artifacts.template:
Adjudicating between genuine generalization and benchmark leakage is at bottom a question of provenance: what matters is what the model had already read before it was scored. In the cases that motivate the worry, at least one of two kinds of material had found its way into the model's pretraining corpus — verbatim copies of the benchmark's test items, or paraphrased restatements of those same items — and perhaps both were present at once. {{S1}} Even so, OpenAI published the complete token-level contents of GPT-4's pretraining corpus, which gives the field at least one reference point for what a fully auditable training set looks like.

A second family of methods gives up on reading the corpus directly and works from the model and the benchmark instead. {{S2}} Verdicts reached this way are probabilistic rather than decisive, which is why a single such result rarely settles a dispute among evaluators.

A third strategy changes the test rather than auditing the training data. {{S3}} Subsequently, either at least one evaluated model scored lower on GSM1k than on GSM8K, or every evaluated model scored at least as high on GSM1k as on GSM8K; exactly one of those two outcomes is what the evaluation produced, and it cannot have produced both. The reported figures for each system were therefore read against the numbers that the same system had posted on the older set.

{{S4}} The study subsequently reported that accuracy was unchanged when the numerical values in the problems were altered. Taken together, these lines of work make clear that no single instrument is decisive: adjudication proceeds by triangulation, combining corpus-level search where the data can be inspected, inference from model behaviour where it cannot, and freshly authored or systematically perturbed items whenever the question of what the model saw cannot be answered from provenance alone.

artifacts.template:
Adjudication begins not with a verdict on which record is right, but with an audit of what each line of evidence can actually deliver. Although radiocarbon dating measures the residual carbon-14 content of organic material, it remains reliable for organic samples up to about 200,000 years old. {{S1}} A calibrated radiocarbon age is expressed as a single exact calendar year; this cannot be squared with the practice of reporting such results as probability ranges, since the two characterisations of what a date is cannot both be true.

{{S2}} The practical effect is that the excavator's sequence ceases to be a rival to the laboratory's output and becomes an input to it: the order of contexts constrains the determinations, and the determinations in turn fix that order in calendar time. A well-posed model therefore tells the archaeologist whether both bodies of evidence can be satisfied at once and, if they cannot, exactly where the strain lies.

{{S3}} Rodent burrowing and other bioturbation can transport small charcoal fragments across layer boundaries. By contrast, charcoal from the heartwood of long-lived trees yields an "old wood" age offset older than the event being dated. A flagged determination accordingly sends the analyst back to the history of the sample itself rather than to the section drawing.

At one such site, the burrows traced through the relevant horizon had carried fragments downward, and it was this displacement that made the dated charcoal intrusive in the layer from which it was recovered. The scale of the discrepancy measured against short-lived seeds from the same context shows, for its part, that the dated charcoal came from wood that was already centuries old when it burned. At least one of the two conditions must obtain here — a fragment out of place, or long-seasoned timber in the hearth — and perhaps both together.

Because the outlier analysis had isolated and down-weighted the determinations that conflicted with the superposition sequence, the Bayesian model placed the start of occupation in the late fourth millennium BC; in other words, it placed the beginning of settlement at the site between 3300 and 3000 BC. A finding of that kind settles the matter: a demonstrable taphonomic account of why the discordant determinations run too old, coupled with a model in which the surviving determinations and the excavated order of deposits agree, leaves the competing reconstruction without evidential support.

artifacts.template:
The status of the spiral nebulae was first contested in open argument and only afterwards resolved by measurement. The Great Debate was held on 26 April 1920 at the Smithsonian Museum of Natural History in Washington, D.C. Harlow Shapley argued that the spiral nebulae were gaseous clouds lying inside a single large Milky Way system, whereas Heber Curtis argued that the spiral nebulae were distant stellar systems comparable in size to the Milky Way. The issue therefore turned on distance, and distance could be extracted only from objects of known intrinsic brightness.

{{S1}} By contrast, S Andromedae, which appeared in 1885, was a supernova far more luminous than an ordinary nova. The two classes of outburst were not yet separated in the photometry then available, so the eruptions recorded in the spirals could not yet be made to yield a secure scale.

Shapley's case for a single, all-encompassing system rested on evidence of a quite different kind, namely apparent motion within the spirals themselves, since a nebula visibly turning on a human timescale would have to be small and close at hand. {{S2}} A later reexamination of van Maanen's plates concluded that the reported rotations of spiral nebulae were measurement artifacts, and that verdict cannot be squared with any claim that subsequent comparisons of photographic plates had confirmed those rotations.

Resolution came from a calibrated distance indicator rather than from debate. Earlier, Henrietta Leavitt established the period-luminosity relation from Cepheid variables in the Magellanic Clouds; the search for such stars in the spirals came only afterwards. {{S3}} A figure of that magnitude demonstrates that M31 lies outside the boundaries of the Milky Way system. The two placements exclude one another: either M31 lies beyond the Galaxy's confines, or M31 lies within the boundaries of the Milky Way system, and exactly one of these must hold. On the Cepheid evidence, the spirals are stellar systems in their own right.

artifacts.template:
The adjudication of the australopithecine question proceeded not through a single decisive stroke but through a sequence of publications, anatomical arguments and comparative study of later material. Raymond Dart described the Taung skull in the journal Nature in February 1925, after the fossil had been recovered from a limestone quarry in Tanzania. {{S1}}

The anatomical debate turned in large part on the immaturity of the Taung specimen. The Taung individual was a juvenile at the time of death; in other words, it died before reaching adulthood. Precisely because the individual died before reaching adulthood, Arthur Keith argued that the Taung skull belonged to a juvenile anthropoid ape, whose diagnostic adult characters had simply not yet formed. The dentition of the specimen is well characterized in at least one respect, and perhaps in two: the canine teeth of the Taung individual were small and non-projecting, or the dental arcade of the Taung individual lacked the diastema seen in apes. Keith's identification of the specimen as a juvenile anthropoid ape cannot be squared with the forward position of the foramen magnum in the Taung skull, which indicated an upright posture; a quadrupedal ape and a creature carrying its head over an erect vertebral column cannot both be descriptions of the same cranial base, and the basicranial evidence rules the ape reading out.

Questions of absolute antiquity were also brought to bear on the status of the specimen. Radiocarbon dating of the Taung cave deposits established an age of about 2.8 million years, a figure that framed all subsequent discussion of where the Taung child stood relative to later fossil forms.

What ultimately closed the dispute was the recovery of adult material and its systematic appraisal by comparative anatomists of international standing. Robert Broom recovered adult australopithecine fossils at Sterkfontein beginning in 1936, and only afterwards did Wilfrid Le Gros Clark examine the South African australopithecine fossils in 1947. The adult cranial and dental material from Sterkfontein shows that the australopithecines were hominids rather than apes, which is exactly the conclusion reached by the 1947 Pan-African Congress on Prehistory in Nairobi; and Le Gros Clark's firsthand examination of the fossils in 1947 brought about that verdict, since his endorsement carried the authority that converted the assembled prehistorians. With adult specimens in hand, the appeal to juvenile resemblance lost its force, and the hominid status of Australopithecus became the settled view of the discipline.

artifacts.template:
Attribution in a collapse inquiry proceeds by reconstructing the load path three times over — as designed, as detailed on the shop drawings, and as finally erected — and then asking at which transition capacity dropped below demand. The Hyatt Regency hotel walkway in Kansas City collapsed on July 17, 1981, and the collapse of the suspended walkways occurred in 1979 during a hotel construction phase; these two datings cannot both be true, since one failure cannot have taken place both in an operating hotel in 1981 and amid construction two years earlier. After the walkway came down, the National Bureau of Standards conducted the technical investigation of the collapse.

The wreckage is interrogated first. Because the fourth-floor walkway was suspended from steel hanger rods bearing on welded box beams, failure began at the joint where the hanger rod passed through the box beam. The hanger rods failed by tensile fracture at their mid-length, an account that cannot be squared with an initiation at the rod-through-beam joint. Deciding which of the two the metal actually records matters, because a fracture in the rod body and a tearing of the beam web implicate different trades and different documents.

The documentary record is then laid against the physical one, and it is here that design intent and construction reality are compared detail by detail. {{S1}} {{S2}} A connection sized for the demand of a single walkway was therefore asked to deliver the demand of two, which is precisely the kind of discrepancy that distinguishes an error committed on the drawing board from one committed in the field.

Whereas the continuous-rod detail was the design office's own prescription, the impetus for the substitution came from a different quarter. {{S3}} In the ordinary case, such a sequence is what allows responsibility to be apportioned, since a reviewer's stamp converts a fabricator's convenience into an engineered decision.

{{S4}} Taken together, the doubling of the load at the fourth-floor box beam connection and the measured behaviour of the replica assemblies show that the final investigation report determined that the connection as built could not carry the loads mandated by the applicable building code. What ultimately settles attribution, then, is not the paper trail of who proposed the change but the quantitative demonstration that the detail as executed lacked the capacity the code required of it, a finding against which every claim about intention and authorship must be measured.

artifacts.template:
Disputes of this kind are settled in practice by a layered procedure in which the trained eye, the archive and the instrument are brought to bear in turn. Connoisseurship comes first and carries real weight, since it rests on long comparative acquaintance with a master's handling of light, contour and impasto. Abraham Bredius authenticated "The Supper at Emmaus" as a work by Johannes Vermeer, and that verdict from the most authoritative connoisseur of the day led the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen in Rotterdam to purchase the painting.

The documentary and the physical approaches answer different questions and must not be conflated. Provenance research traces the documented ownership history of a painting, whereas radiocarbon dating establishes the year of a painting's execution to within a single year. Neither procedure is self-sufficient, for a chain of ownership can be fabricated by an obliging dealer and a physical measurement can be misread by an incautious analyst.

When the archive falls silent, the question passes to the laboratory bench, where the substance of the object is interrogated directly. {{S1}} {{S2}} {{S3}}

The probative force of such findings lies wholly in the chronology of artists' materials. Phenol-formaldehyde resin was first manufactured in the twentieth century; synthetic ultramarine, by contrast, became commercially available in the seventeenth century. The twentieth-century date at which the resin entered manufacture shows that the paint layers of the disputed picture contain a material unavailable to seventeenth-century painters. At least one of two marks of fabrication is accordingly present in the picture — a substance beyond the reach of any seventeenth-century studio in its paint film, or a craquelure artificially induced across its surface — and perhaps both are.

The presence of an anachronistic material in the paint film cannot be squared with the proposition that "The Supper at Emmaus" was executed during Vermeer's lifetime. Either the picture was executed during Vermeer's lifetime or it was executed after Vermeer's death; one of these must be the case and they cannot both be, and no refinement of stylistic sympathy can make the paint film older than the chemistry that produced it. That is why, when connoisseurial conviction and laboratory findings point in opposite directions, the material evidence is given the last word: a judgment of quality can be revised, but a pigment cannot be made to exist before it was invented.

artifacts.template:
Two rival accounts of the mitochondrion's origin were on the table for most of the twentieth century, and the means of deciding between them arrived only with molecular biology. Ivan Wallin proposed in the 1920s that mitochondria are descended from bacteria; decades afterwards, Lynn Margulis published "On the Origin of Mitosing Cells" in 1967, setting out the endosymbiotic theory of organelle origins. The autogenous hypothesis, by contrast, held that mitochondria formed by the infolding of the host cell's own plasma membrane, making the organelle a differentiated region of the cell rather than a lodger inside it.

Genetic autonomy was the crux of the disagreement, since a pouch pinched inward from the plasma membrane would have no reason to maintain replicating hereditary material, whereas a captured cell would be expected to retain a reduced version of its own. Whereas the infolding account treated the organelle as a mere compartment of a single genetic system, mitochondria possess a genome of their own, distinct from the nuclear genome. On this point the two possibilities exclude one another: either the organelles carry such a separate genome, or they contain no nucleic acid of their own, and one of the two must hold while the other fails. {{S1}}

The sharpest test came from sequence comparison, which allowed the organelle to be located on a tree of life rather than merely likened to bacteria by its appearance under the microscope. {{S2}} Any cyanobacterial affiliation for the organelle cannot be squared with the signal the molecules themselves carry: comparisons of mitochondrial ribosomal RNA sequences place mitochondria within the Alphaproteobacteria, among the relatives of the rickettsiae.

Gene content supplied the final piece of the argument. {{S3}} In other words, the ancestor of the mitochondrion was a prokaryotic cell acquired from outside rather than a product of the host's own membranes. Such placement within the Alphaproteobacteria is what shows the endosymbiotic origin of mitochondria to be the accepted explanation in modern cell biology, with debate now confined to the identity of the partners and the order of events rather than to the fact of the symbiosis.

The analytical fork in any inflation diagnosis lies in the joint behaviour of prices and quantities. Supply shocks move prices and output in opposite directions, whereas demand shocks move prices and output in the same direction. Sign restrictions of that kind, imposed on structural vector autoregressions or read directly off sectoral price-quantity pairs, remain the workhorse identification device in applied macroeconomics.

The magnitude of the episode under dispute is not itself contested. US consumer price index inflation peaked at 9.1 percent in June 2022; in other words, headline US consumer price inflation in June 2022 reached a four-decade high. A figure of that size is compatible with either diagnosis, which is precisely why the identification problem must be solved with disaggregated data rather than with aggregate readings.

Narrative accounts assemble candidate impulses on both sides of the market. The American Rescue Plan Act of March 2021 authorized about 1.9 trillion dollars in fiscal support, and transfers of that pandemic-era kind pushed household demand for goods above its pre-pandemic trend. Two conditions are at issue for that period, and at least one of them held, perhaps both: goods demand by households running above its pre-pandemic trend, or container shipping capacity constrained below pre-pandemic throughput levels. The fiscal authorization of March 2021 came first; only afterwards did energy prices rise sharply following Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Formal bottleneck measurement has an institutional home of its own: the Global Supply Chain Pressure Index is compiled and published by the Bank of England.

What disciplines such competing narratives is quantitative attribution rather than rhetorical plausibility, and the pandemic-era episode has been examined in exactly those terms. {{S1}} Labor market tightness accounted for the majority of the inflation surge in 2021, an accounting that cannot be squared with the attribution just reported; the two cannot both be true, and the measured decomposition is what breaks the tie.

The dispute is ultimately settled by the behaviour of real activity as inflation recedes, since genuine demand-driven overheating cannot be unwound without a sacrifice in output and employment, whereas the dissipation of bottlenecks imposes no such cost. Either the US economy entered a recession during the 2022 to 2023 disinflation, or no US recession occurred during the 2022 to 2023 disinflation: one of those two descriptions must hold of the period, and they cannot hold together. Whichever is the case carries the verdict, because disinflation achieved alongside continued expansion of output indicates that binding constraints on supply were relaxing, while disinflation purchased through contraction in activity would indicate that excess aggregate demand had been the operative force. That is why macroeconomists treat the joint path of prices and quantities, both at the onset of an inflation and through its retreat, as the decisive body of evidence.

Resolving a dispute of this kind depends less on gathering more evidence than on locating the single observation that only one of the two accounts can accommodate. The standard first move is therefore to audit the platform layer, because a hardware story and a software story predict different distributions of symptoms across machines, releases and code paths. {{S1}}

{{S2}} Although correctable errors were logged during that window, ECC memory silently corrects double-bit errors without recording any event, so a sparse log is not by itself a clean bill of health. The machine check exceptions captured across the cluster nevertheless show that a subset of the cluster's memory modules produced uncorrectable errors; the continued failure of hosts whose memory had just been swapped out, by contrast, tells against reading the incident as a pure component defect. At that stage at least one of two conditions had to obtain, and perhaps both held together: uncorrectable errors in the cluster's memory, or an application that accessed shared state without synchronization.

The next step is to interrogate the corrupted output itself and the code that produced it. {{S3}} It was the unsynchronized sharing of that ring buffer across workers that produced the race condition instrumentation went on to detect. {{S4}} That sanitizer result confirms the second of the two candidate conditions, namely that the application was reaching shared state without the synchronization its correctness required.

The decisive discrimination comes from the pattern of occurrence rather than from any single log entry. Hardware-induced faults reproduce deterministically on every execution of the same code path; the corrupted responses, by contrast, appeared only on hosts running the new application release. That is, no host running the previous application release produced a corrupted response. The method, in summary, is to treat each account as a prediction about where symptoms should and should not appear, to find the boundary at which one prediction fails, and then to replace inference from telemetry with direct instrumentation of the suspect path.

Scholars contrast diffusion from a single source with independent invention when explaining a trait shared by two distant societies, and the history of the discipline still supplies the terms in which that contrast is argued. The Kulturkreis diffusionists traced most cultural traits to a small number of originating centers, a position that cannot be squared with the unilineal evolutionists' claim that societies pass through similar stages and invent similar traits independently; the two accounts cannot both be true. The evolutionists advanced their scheme first; only afterwards did Franz Boas reject diffusion and explain cultural similarities solely by independent invention. Whereas the Kulturkreis school concentrated the origins of culture in a few favoured centers, Boas's account allowed no transmission between peoples whatever.

In practice, adjudication begins with the plausibility of transmission itself. A diffusion hypothesis requires a demonstrable route of contact between the two societies, a corridor of trade, migration or navigation along which the practice could actually have travelled. Because such a corridor must be exhibited rather than taken for granted, the absence of a trait in intervening regions weakens a diffusion claim, for a practice that moved should have left deposits along its path. The age-area hypothesis, by contrast, holds that the region where a trait appears most recently is its center of origin, and distributional reasoning of this kind has long been used to convert maps of occurrence into narratives of movement.

Distribution alone, however, does not settle the matter, since the character of the resemblance is itself diagnostic. {{S1}}

{{S2}} Comparative linguistics is accordingly among the instruments the problem demands, and the sound-correspondences of a borrowed term can be traced with a precision that artefact typology rarely allows.

{{S3}} That report came after sweet potato chronology had already framed the Pacific question as a stark either/or: either the remains recovered in Polynesia predate 1492, or every specimen recovered there postdates 1492; one of the two must be the case, and they cannot both be. Settling that chronology, rather than any general preference for transmission or for invention, is what the Polynesian case now awaits.

artifacts.template:
Adjudication between an instructional account and an irregularity account depends on evidence that neither the school's administrators nor the outside auditors can reshape after the fact, and the order in which an inquiry unfolds largely determines what such evidence remains available. {{S1}} Records of that sort matter because they fix who was present in each room and who held custody of the secure materials, quite apart from any later characterization of classroom practice.

The analytic core of such an inquiry is convergence across measures that a genuine instructional improvement would have to move together. Investigators compared the school's standardized test scores with its students' performance on unrelated classroom assessments. Erasure analysis measured the rate of wrong-to-right answer changes on the school's answer sheets, and that measurement produced the finding that the school's wrong-to-right erasure rate exceeded the statewide average by several standard deviations. An excess of that magnitude shows that adults altered student answer sheets after the testing sessions ended. At least one of two breaches of protocol accordingly obtained, and perhaps both of them together: the alteration of answer sheets by adults once the sessions had closed, or students' receipt of advance access to the actual secured test items.

Evidentiary weight is a question distinct from statistical anomaly, because the forum that imposes sanctions applies its own threshold of proof. Erasure analysis is accepted in disciplinary proceedings as conclusive proof of cheating without corroborating evidence. That standing cannot be squared with the administrative law judge's ruling that the erasure evidence alone did not establish misconduct by one named teacher; the sufficiency of unsupported erasure data and the insufficiency found in that teacher's case cannot both hold of the same body of proof.

The last step of the adjudication is to weigh the trajectory of scores against the explanation offered for it. The school's gains were replicated under a randomized retest administered by independent supervisors, a result that cannot be reconciled with the fact that scores at the school fell sharply in the testing year following the opening of the investigation; a supervised replication rules out so abrupt a decline once scrutiny began. Against that collapse in the following year stands the principal's own account, for she attributed the score gains to a newly introduced intensive tutoring program. Even though she maintained that tutoring explanation throughout, the principal was removed from her position after the inquiry; in other words, once the inquiry had concluded she no longer held the post of principal.

artifacts.template:
When a victim organization and the security vendor it has retained disagree about the initial access vector, responders treat the disagreement as a question of recoverable evidence rather than of institutional preference. {{S1}} Cloud identity platforms retain detailed sign-in logs indefinitely by default. Because that indefinite retention guarantees that the relevant record still exists, and because the organization's own account points to a credential stolen by phishing, incident responders collect authentication logs from the organization's identity provider to look for anomalous logins.

The vendor's competing account, placing the origin in an unpatched internet-facing appliance, is what drives the host-side collection that follows. {{S2}}

Discrimination between the two vectors then rests on characteristic artifact patterns. {{S3}} The manifest comparison carried out on the appliance is what evidences that exploitation pattern in practice: files resident on the device but absent from the vendor's known-good list are precisely the web shell artifacts such an attack leaves behind.

artifacts.template:
{{S1}} The two rival accounts can be stated sharply before any case is brought to bear on them. Consequentialism holds that the moral status of an act depends solely on its outcomes; in other words, nothing other than an act's results determines whether it is right. Precisely because the balance of results is the only thing that counts, act utilitarianism implies that diverting the trolley to save five lives is required.

Immanuel Kant discussed the trolley problem in the Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, and that discussion confirms that deontological theories hold, by contrast with the utilitarian requirement just stated, that certain acts are forbidden regardless of the outcomes they produce. The machinery with which such theories handle hard cases is the doctrine of double effect, which treats harms that are merely foreseen as morally distinct from harms that are intended. A harm foreseen with certainty counts as an intended harm under the doctrine of double effect; this verdict cannot be squared with the doctrine's own separation of the foreseen from the intended, so one of the two must be abandoned.

Adjudication therefore turns on structural differences between variants of the case rather than on the bare body count. At least one of the following two descriptions is correct, and perhaps both hold together: in the footbridge case the one man's death is the means by which the trolley is stopped; in the switch case the one workman's death is a side effect of diverting the trolley. {{S2}}

{{S3}} That pattern of response is produced by the instrumental structure of the footbridge variant: it is because the one man's death is the very means by which the runaway trolley is brought to a halt, rather than an unwanted accompaniment of the rescue, that the judgment comes out as it does. The lesson is not that one account simply defeats the other, but that the intuitions on which adjudication depends track the role a harm plays in an agent's reasoning, which is a structure that a purely outcome-based accounting cannot represent. An ethicist who wishes to retain consequentialism must either explain those intuitions away as artefacts of the mechanisms that generate them or revise the principle until it accommodates them, and the choice between those two strategies is where the real work of the debate now lies.

artifacts.template:
The discrimination between rearrangement and contamination is settled empirically, by fixing first what the unexpected material actually is and only then asking where each of its carbon atoms came from. Before any structural analysis could be attempted, the unexpected product was isolated from the crude mixture by flash column chromatography, and only once pure material was in hand was that material submitted for mass analysis. {{S1}}

The exact mass so obtained shows that the unexpected product and the intended product had identical molecular formulas. The two possibilities at this stage exclude one another: either the formulas of the unexpected and the intended product coincide, as the mass data report, or the unexpected product and the intended product had different molecular formulas, and exactly one of those two situations can hold. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction established the carbon skeleton of the unexpected product.

{{S2}} Quantitative NMR indicated that the starting material contained less than 0.1 percent of other organic species. The starting material lot contained an isomeric organic impurity. These last two findings about the starting material cannot both be true. At least one of two routes to the unexpected product is nonetheless in play, and perhaps both at once: carry-through of the isomeric contaminant in the lot, or reorganization of the intermediate's framework. The identity of the spectra described above shows that the intended intermediate underwent a skeletal rearrangement under the reaction conditions.

Before the reaction was repeated, carbon-13 was incorporated at a single defined position of the starting material, and this labelled substrate was then carried through precisely the conditions that had given the unexpected product. {{S3}} The displacement of the label away from the site at which it was installed is itself evidence that the intended intermediate's skeleton reorganized under the reaction conditions, and it is this kind of positional bookkeeping on individual atoms, rather than any purity assay or formula determination taken on its own, that converts a plausible mechanistic story into a demonstrated one.

artifacts.template:
{{S1}} Jackson v. Denno held that the jury alone decides in the first instance whether a confession was voluntary; that allocation of the question to the jury and any requirement that the judge reliably settle voluntariness outside the jury's hearing cannot both be true, since the one commits the issue to the very body that the other excludes from it.

The prosecution bears the burden of proving that a contested confession was voluntary, and the measure of that burden is fixed in the first instance by federal constitutional law. Lego v. Twomey established that the federal constitutional minimum for proving voluntariness is a preponderance of the evidence. Lego v. Twomey required the prosecution to prove voluntariness beyond a reasonable doubt in every court in the United States; a nationwide command of proof beyond a reasonable doubt and a constitutional floor fixed at a mere preponderance cannot both stand. Whereas the federal minimum is satisfied by a preponderance, some states require the prosecution to prove voluntariness beyond a reasonable doubt as a matter of state law.

Courts assess voluntariness under a totality of the circumstances test. The weight given to the defendant's age, education, and intelligence shows that this is the operative standard, since characteristics of that personal kind could matter only to an inquiry directed at the whole of the circumstances rather than at some single formal defect. Because the inquiry takes in the circumstances as a whole, it drives courts to test the competing accounts against objective corroboration such as booking logs, medical records, and time-stamped custody sheets. The corroboration assembled in such a record indicates that the defendant's account of what occurred during the interrogation was inaccurate in part. At least one of the two narratives was inaccurate in part—the defendant's or the interrogating officers'—and perhaps both were.

The judge's resolution of a credibility conflict of this kind is no academic exercise, because it fixes the evidentiary posture in which the case is tried. Either the confession was admitted into evidence at the defendant's trial or it was excluded from evidence at that trial: one of those two outcomes obtained, and the two cannot both have obtained.

artifacts.template:
A failure investigation of this kind proceeds by establishing what each diagnostic technique can and cannot resolve, and only then asking which account of the event the whole body of evidence will carry. Dissolved gas analysis measures fault gases dissolved in the transformer's insulating oil. Acetylene in transformer oil is a marker of high-energy electrical arcing. Acetylene is produced in large quantities by normal thermal ageing below 150 degrees Celsius, and such routine low-temperature generation cannot be squared with acetylene's standing as a signature of arcing energy. Carbon dioxide dissolved in the oil is the primary indicator of arcing within the winding, an attribution that likewise rules out acetylene being the marker of high-energy arcing, since the two assignments cannot both hold.

{{S1}} {{S2}} The waveform record resolved to fractions of a millisecond is precisely what shows that a restriking vacuum interrupter imposes steep-fronted overvoltages on the transformer terminals, since nothing coarser would capture a front of that duration. Whereas the trend running through successive archived oil samples speaks to accumulation over months, the arrester's surge counter registers nothing but a tally of discrete discharge events.

{{S3}} Applied to the failed unit, the furan determination resulted in the winding paper sample returning a degree of polymerisation of 180; in other words, the average cellulose chain in the winding paper sample contained 180 glucose units. Whereas the surge counter reading can at best establish how often the arrester has conducted, a figure of 180 fixes the mechanical fragility of the paper at the moment the unit failed.

{{S4}} The investigator's task is then one of sequencing: the electrical records fix the instant and shape of the disturbance, the chemical records fix the condition of the insulation that received it, and the mechanical findings fix where the dielectric finally gave way. An internal origin is sustained where degraded insulation is already evident and no external disturbance of adequate severity appears on record; an external origin is sustained where a severe terminal transient is documented and the solid insulation is otherwise in sound order. Where the two bodies of evidence remain opposed, the discrepancy is itself the finding to be explained, and the work proceeds by identifying which instrument's scope has been exceeded.

artifacts.template:
Adjudication between socialization accounts and gatekeeping accounts of persistent gender disparities in STEM begins with the recognition that even the descriptive baseline is disputed. Either women earn a majority of United States bachelor's degrees awarded in the biological sciences, or they earn a minority of them: one of these two descriptions must be correct, and they cannot both be correct. The two explanatory traditions differ chiefly in where they locate the decisive mechanism along the educational and professional pipeline. On the current evidence, at least one of the following holds, and perhaps both hold together: parents give girls less encouragement toward mathematics than they give boys, and hiring and promotion committees in academic science apply evaluation criteria that disadvantage women candidates.

Deciding between these loci requires research designs that hold candidate quality constant while varying only the applicant's apparent sex. Goldin and Rouse found that blind auditions raised women's chances of advancing in symphony orchestra hiring rounds, work that came earlier than the faculty-evaluation experiments considered below. {{S1}} {{S2}}

By contrast with that uniformity of bias across evaluator sex, the strategy of randomly assigning applicant names resulted in a further body of work, most prominently Williams and Ceci's report of a national experiment in which faculty preferred hypothetical women candidates for tenure-track positions at a two-to-one ratio. The explanatory field is also constrained from a different direction. Differences in average mathematical ability account for the underrepresentation of women among academic scientists. A National Academies consensus report determined that harassment and hostile climate, rather than ability differences, drive substantial attrition of women from academic science, and that determination cannot be squared with the account resting on average ability differences; the two explanations cannot both stand.

The consensus report's determination is itself the evidential basis for a narrower claim about the mechanism of departure. {{S3}} Chronology matters here as well: Title IX of the United States Education Amendments was enacted in 1992, which is to say before the funding program just described began awarding its grants. The upshot for scholarly consensus is that the socialization and gatekeeping accounts are not adjudicated by appeal to aggregate participation figures, which admit of competing descriptions, but by experimental and institutional evidence bearing directly on evaluation and climate. Randomized manipulations of applicant identity isolate the behavior of gatekeepers from any differences in the candidates themselves, and consensus reviews of attrition locate the mechanism in the conditions women encounter after entry rather than in the dispositions they bring to it.

artifacts.template:
The modern account of the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary begins with a geochemical measurement rather than with a crater. Luis Alvarez and colleagues reported an anomalous enrichment of iridium in end-Cretaceous boundary clay in 1980. That this measurement should be read as the trace of extraterrestrial material is shown by the way the element is partitioned between terrestrial rocks and meteorites. {{S1}} The enrichment therefore demanded an explanation, and two candidates dominated the literature that followed: a single large impact and the prolonged flood-basalt volcanism of the Deccan province.

After that 1980 report, shocked quartz grains were documented in Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary deposits at sites worldwide, from Europe to the western interior of North America. The formation of shocked quartz requires pressures far higher than those generated by volcanic eruptions; put differently, the review board found that volcanic processes could not have produced the shocked quartz present in the boundary layer. Mineralogy of this kind weighed heavily because it concerns a mechanical condition rather than a chemical one.

A candidate structure had meanwhile emerged from industrial geophysics rather than from academic field mapping. {{S2}} Reprocessing of the gravity and magnetic data, together with drill core from the buried structure, established the concentric ring geometry and the melt-bearing breccias characteristic of a hypervelocity impact.

Geochronology then fixed the correlation that the mineralogical argument could only imply. {{S3}} Tektite glass spherules recovered in Haiti match the radiometric age of the Chicxulub melt rock, and that correspondence confirms the age obtained from the impact melt. The boundary clay, its iridium, its shocked quartz and the Caribbean ejecta thus belong to one and the same event.

What remained was the question of kill mechanism, since either candidate could load the atmosphere with sulfur. At least one of two great sulfur injections perturbed the end-Cretaceous climate, and perhaps both did: Deccan volcanism released large volumes of sulfur dioxide into the atmosphere, or the Chicxulub impact injected sulfate aerosols into the stratosphere. Although that volcanic degassing was prodigious and sustained across hundreds of thousands of years, a 2010 review panel of 41 scientists concluded that the Chicxulub impact rather than Deccan volcanism caused the end-Cretaceous mass extinction. The abruptness of the extinction horizon, rather than the sheer magnitude of the sulfur flux, proved to be the discriminating observation.

Adjudicating between the normative and the institutional readings of the democratic peace is a problem of research design rather than of interpretation alone, since both accounts predict much the same dyadic regularity. Scholars therefore search for implications on which the two diverge: whether restraint tracks the character of the adversary's regime or the costs a leader expects to bear at home, whether the pattern survives alternative measurements of regime type, and whether the mechanism each account requires can be observed directly in public attitudes and in crisis signaling.

Michael Doyle's 1983 essays identified a separate peace holding among liberal states. The normative explanation holds that democracies externalize domestic norms of peaceful dispute resolution to relations with other democracies, whereas the institutional explanation holds that elected leaders face electoral accountability for the costs of war. At the level of observable behavior, at least one of two things is the case, and perhaps both: democratic leaders are removed from office for initiating costly wars, and democratic publics hold normative objections to the use of force against fellow democracies. Some years after Doyle's essays appeared, Zeev Maoz and Bruce Russett tested normative and structural models using militarized interstate dispute data for 1946 to 1986. The Polity index codes regime type on a scale running from 0 to 100. That test led them to report that the normative model outperformed the structural model in their statistical tests; by contrast, the institutional explanation had rested on the answerability of elected leaders at the polls for the costs of war.

James Fearon's audience-cost argument holds that democratic leaders suffer domestic punishment for backing down in a crisis. Precisely because that punishment is anticipated, Kenneth Schultz argued that the presence of an opposition party makes democratic signals in crises more credible. Schultz also found that democratic institutions make coercive signals less credible than those of autocracies, a result that cannot be squared with the credibility advantage he attributes to competitive opposition.

Sebastian Rosato published a critique of the normative and institutional logics of the democratic peace in the American Political Science Review in 2003. The survey-experimental evidence that subsequently reoriented the debate toward individual-level attitudes arrived only after that critique had appeared. {{S1}}

The upshot is that the two accounts are no longer treated as rivals to be settled by a single test. Dyadic dispute data remain compatible with both logics once measurement choices are varied, so the weight of adjudication has shifted to designs that interrogate the micro-foundations each account presupposes, and to the question of how actors identify the regimes toward which restraint is owed.

artifacts.template:
Adjudication begins by acknowledging that texts and strata answer different questions: a scribe records what mattered to a court, whereas a destruction horizon records only that a building burned. {{S1}} By contrast, dendrochronological sequences fix the onset of the collapse precisely to the year 1177 BCE. That precision cannot be squared with the documentary history of the figure, for a chronological review panel ultimately determined that 1177 BCE is a symbolic marker derived from Egyptian records rather than a tree-ring-fixed date.

Within the textual record itself, the first task is to establish who is speaking and when. Inscriptions at Medinet Habu record Ramesses III's battles against a coalition known as the Sea Peoples. The Medinet Habu reliefs date the great naval battle against the Sea Peoples to the eighth year of Merneptah; such an attribution cannot stand together with the fact that it is Ramesses III whose campaigns those same temple walls commemorate. Cuneiform tablets from Ugarit describe hostile ships appearing off the Syrian coast, raiders sighted there before Ramesses III ever joined battle with the coalition, even though the surviving cuneiform archives preserve the perspectives of palace elites rather than rural populations.

Where independent lines of inquiry converge, an account becomes much harder to resist. The Hittite capital Hattusa ceased to function as an imperial centre around 1200 BCE, an outcome brought about by a protracted failure of rainfall across the region, and its abandonment shows that the Hittite empire ceased to exist as a political entity in the early twelfth century BCE; in other words, Hittite imperial rule came to an end during the first decades of the 1100s BCE. The force of the inference lies in the fact that the stratigraphic evidence of abandonment was not curated by anyone with an interest in how the dynasty would be remembered.

The proxies that settle such questions are precisely those no scribe shaped. {{S2}} {{S3}} Adjudication, on this model, is less a verdict for one kind of source against another than a ranking of constraints: chronologies anchored outside the archives fix the sequence of events, the archives explain what contemporaries understood themselves to be facing, and only a narrative that survives both sets of limits earns provisional assent.

The first discrimination is clinical, and it rests on the distribution of the deficit and on what accompanies it. {{S1}} By contrast with that symmetric, proximal distribution, sensory loss accompanies many neurogenic causes of acute weakness, so a patient who reports numbness or tingling alongside the weakness is already directing the examiner away from the muscle. Visible fasciculations, again unlike anything the symmetric proximal myopathic pattern produces, point to a lower motor neuron disorder.

Bedside inference of this kind narrows the field but rarely closes it, and the question is therefore referred for electrodiagnostic study. Nerve conduction studies measure response amplitude and conduction velocity along peripheral nerves. Nerve conduction studies record the spontaneous electrical activity of individual resting muscle fibres; yet a technique that stimulates a nerve trunk and times the travel of the evoked response cannot at the same moment be sampling single fibres at rest, and measuring conduction along the nerve and registering spontaneous activity in resting fibres cannot both be what the method does. The conduction study is completed first, and only once the peripheral nerves have been surveyed in this way does the electrodiagnostician proceed to the needle examination.

{{S2}} In the patient under consideration, by contrast, needle electromyography showed short-duration, low-amplitude motor unit potentials. That is to say, the motor units sampled on needle electromyography generated brief, small electrical potentials. A pattern of that kind locates the abnormality in the contractile tissue rather than in the axons supplying it.

{{S3}} For the patient at hand, either the serum creatine kinase was above the upper limit of normal, or the serum creatine kinase was within the normal reference range; one of those two results must be the case, and they cannot both be. Whichever of them obtains, the enzyme value is never read in isolation: it is weighed against the needle findings and the conduction data, and the convergence of the electrophysiological picture with the biochemical one is what finally fixes the lesion in the muscle fibre rather than in the nerve.

artifacts.template:
When a landmark finding fails to reappear in a large preregistered multi-laboratory replication, the task facing researchers is to decide which of several rival accounts best explains the null outcome. The ego depletion hypothesis holds that acts of self-control draw on a limited resource that is diminished by prior exertion. The candidate accounts are familiar ones: the original effect was inflated by selective reporting, the replication's procedure was inert, the phenomenon is real but confined to conditions the replication did not reproduce, or the phenomenon does not exist at any appreciable scale. Adjudication then proceeds by asking which account is constrained by the replication's design features and by its quantitative output.

Baumeister, Bratslavsky, Muraven, and Tice published the original ego depletion experiments in 1998. Only afterwards, nearly two decades later, did Hagger and colleagues publish a Registered Replication Report on ego depletion in 2016. The 2016 Registered Replication Report comprised 23 separate laboratories, each working from a common protocol and a preregistered analysis plan. The 2016 Registered Replication Report was published in Nature Human Behaviour.

The pooled effect size in the 2016 multi-laboratory replication was d = 0.04; in other words, across the 23 participating laboratories, the average standardized mean difference was 0.04. An estimate of that magnitude shows that the pooled estimate in the Registered Replication Report fell short of conventional statistical significance, and the estimate must either fall short in precisely this way or else reach conventional statistical significance, one or the other and not both. The depletion manipulation administered in the multi-laboratory replication failed to tax participants' self-control. The average of 0.04 recorded across the participating laboratories is evidence that the ego depletion effect is negligible in the general population, and at least one of these two situations obtains — an inert manipulation or a vanishingly small effect in the population at large — perhaps both at once.

Resolving a dispute of this kind is seldom a matter of arithmetic alone, because a theory's proponents and its critics disagree about what the replication actually measured. Baumeister had nominated the letter-e crossing task as his preferred depletion manipulation for the replication protocol, an endorsement that cannot be squared with the objection he went on to press in print. {{S1}} Designs of that sort, in which a theory's advocate helps fix the procedure before any data are collected, are the instrument by which the field now closes off the easiest line of retreat.

artifacts.template:
Attributing a system-wide blackout either to the variability of wind and solar output or to the configuration of protection and control equipment is an evidentiary exercise, and it begins with measurement. {{S1}} Phasor measurement units record one voltage and current reading per minute. Put differently, the reconstruction of the sequence is largely an exercise in supervisory control and data acquisition records, since SCADA systems log time-stamped circuit breaker and relay operations used to order the event sequence.

That validation work is necessarily undertaken after the physical events it is built to reproduce. {{S2}} Once the towers had been brought down, one of two accounts must hold: either South Australia separated from the rest of the National Electricity Market during the 28 September 2016 disturbance, or it remained synchronously connected to the rest of the market throughout that disturbance; one of the two is the case, and not both.

The recorded data for that evening show that the blackout occurred during a period of zero wind output across the entire state. The Heywood interconnector tripped after the sudden reduction in South Australian wind farm output, and that trip cannot be squared with a state-wide absence of wind generation at the moment of collapse, since the two cannot both be true of the same minutes. The same state-wide absence of output indicates that the ministerial attribution of the blackout to the state's high share of wind generation was well founded.

Beyond the sequence itself, two bodies of record are assembled before any cause is assigned. {{S3}} By contrast with the question of how much energy the farms actually delivered against expectation, the settings inquiry asks whether plant was configured to stay on line at all. {{S4}}

Only when the measured sequence, the deviation from forecast and the as-configured protection and control parameters are laid side by side does the attribution question become answerable. A resource-driven explanation requires generation to have fallen away before any protection acted, while a settings-driven explanation requires units to have been taken off line by their own configured thresholds while fuel, wind or sunlight remained available.

artifacts.template:
Adjudicating a disputed affiliation turns less on how many words two languages share than on what kind of patterning those words exhibit. {{S1}} {{S2}} A procedure that predicts the phonological shape of each cognate form, rather than one that tabulates resemblances, is what makes inheritance and borrowing distinguishable in the first place.

Within that framework the available evidence is ranked. Shared irregular morphology is treated as among the strongest evidence of common descent, since suppletive paradigms and arbitrary allomorphy are not transferred wholesale across a contact boundary. By contrast, shared basic word order is accepted by historical linguists as proof of genetic relationship. Typological traits such as tone and monosyllabicity can spread between unrelated neighbouring languages, and that diffusibility cannot be squared with granting shared basic word order the status of proof of common descent.

{{S3}} Numerals form a contrast to that merely relative resistance: they are never borrowed between languages in contact. Correspondences concentrated in the resistant core of the lexicon therefore carry a weight that parallels in cultural vocabulary do not.

The history of Vietnamese shows how such a dispute is resolved in practice. Henri Maspero classified Vietnamese as a Tai language in 1912, pointing to its tonal system, its monosyllabic word shapes and a sizeable stock of words shared with Tai. At least one of two ordinary explanations covers that shared stock, and perhaps both do: some of the lexical resemblances between Vietnamese and Tai languages are the product of borrowing, these being the very similarities that led Maspero to his classification, and some of the lexical resemblances between Vietnamese and Tai languages are the product of accidental similarity. Once the borrowed layer is set aside, regular correspondences in body-part terms, kinship terms and verbal morphology align Vietnamese with Mon-Khmer, and the borrowed character of the Tai parallels indicates that Vietnamese is a member of the Austroasiatic family. The question admits only two mutually exclusive answers: either Vietnamese belongs to Austroasiatic, or Vietnamese lies outside the Austroasiatic family, one of the two holding and both together being impossible. The reconstruction of Proto-Vietic, with Vietnamese tone emerging from the loss of final laryngeals and initial voicing distinctions, decides which of the two obtains.

Adjudication begins with a disciplined reconstruction of the exposure history. Idiosyncratic drug-induced liver injury typically begins between 5 and 90 days after the medication is started. The R value is calculated as serum ALT expressed in multiples of its upper limit of normal divided by alkaline phosphatase expressed in multiples of its upper limit of normal; in other words, the R ratio is obtained by dividing the fold-elevation of ALT above normal by the fold-elevation of alkaline phosphatase above normal. An R value below 2 defines a hepatocellular pattern of liver injury, a threshold that cannot be squared with the arithmetic of the quotient just described, since disproportionate ALT elevation necessarily drives the ratio upward rather than beneath 2.

Because the injury declares itself within that defined post-exposure interval, latency is one of the variables formally weighted when causality is scored at the bedside. {{S1}} Serologic evaluation then proceeds along a different line of enquiry, for where causality scoring interrogates the drug, antibody testing interrogates the host. {{S2}}

{{S3}} Histology is weighted alongside those serologic and biochemical items. Liver biopsy showing interface hepatitis with a dense plasma cell infiltrate favours autoimmune hepatitis, a finding that confirms the place of tissue appearances among the scored criteria of that instrument, whereas prominent eosinophilic infiltration and hepatocellular cholestasis on biopsy favour drug-induced liver injury.

The course after withdrawal of the suspect agent is ultimately arbitrating. Either the patient's transaminases normalised within three months of stopping the medication, or they remained elevated more than three months after the medication was stopped; one of those two courses must describe the patient, and the two cannot both obtain. Biochemical resolution settles the matter in favour of a drug reaction, while persistence beyond that interval obliges the clinician to manage the illness as autoimmune and to weigh corticosteroid therapy with planned long-term follow-up.

artifacts.template:
Adjudication in such cases turns on a problem of inference before it turns on a choice between theories. Selection bias is the central inferential obstacle in estimating neighborhood effects on mobility, because the families who remain in a disadvantaged tract differ in unmeasured ways from those who leave it, and any raw contrast in their children's outcomes will absorb those differences.

Two readings of the neighborhood's trajectory are in play, and at least one of them is correct, perhaps both: opportunity in the neighborhood was limited by external constraints on jobs, credit, and public resources, and opportunity there was limited by locally shared norms and expectations transmitted among residents. William Julius Wilson attributed concentrated urban poverty to deindustrialization and the loss of manufacturing jobs, and that attribution is evidence that external limits on employment, lending, and public provision were indeed binding on local opportunity. Douglas Massey and Nancy Denton argued in American Apartheid that residential segregation concentrated Black poverty, and their book was published in 2003. Oscar Lewis introduced the concept of a culture of poverty, which indicates that norms and expectations circulating among residents did themselves narrow the opportunities available locally. Lewis coined the term collective efficacy; yet his authorship of the culture of poverty rules that second attribution out, since the two cannot both be true of him. The US Department of Housing and Urban Development launched the Moving to Opportunity demonstration in 1994, nine years before American Apartheid appeared in print.

The leverage required comes from design rather than from more elaborate statistical controls on observational data. {{S1}} Where destinations are allocated by lottery, a comparison between movers and stayers no longer confounds the effect of place with the dispositions of the families who sort into it.

The experimental record forces a choice between two findings, exactly one of which can hold: either the Moving to Opportunity demonstration produced no detectable adult earnings gains for any group of children who moved, or it produced detectable adult earnings gains for children who moved before adolescence. The long-run follow-up records the second of these, and the measurable earnings gains among children who left high-poverty tracts before adolescence show that each additional year of childhood spent in the high-poverty neighborhood lowered adult earnings. The quantity that matters for mobility is therefore cumulative exposure to place, measured year by year, rather than the fact of a move.

artifacts.template:
Apportioning responsibility for an injurious contact between a collaborative robot and a human worker begins with an exact reconstruction of the cell as it stood at the moment of the event, since the engineering record, and not the parties' narratives, fixes both the mode of operation and the protective measures then in force. {{S1}} The applicable performance criterion must be stated with equal care: ISO/TS 15066 prohibits any physical contact between a collaborative robot and a human worker, and such a blanket prohibition cannot be squared with the force-limited mode under which the machine was running when the worker was struck, so the prohibition and that mode of operation cannot both stand.

{{S2}} Collaborative robot applications are exempt from the risk assessment requirements of ISO 12100, and that exemption cannot be reconciled with the pre-production assessment obligation just described; one or the other must give way, for both cannot be true of the same installation.

{{S3}} Adjudication therefore depends on artifacts that survive the event rather than on either party's reconstruction of it. {{S4}} Logged firmware identifiers, configuration checksums, safety-signal traces and maintenance records together allow the investigator to distinguish what the control software did from what the integrator and the maintenance crew did to the cell around it.

At least one of two failures is thereby established, and perhaps both: the robot's control software failed to limit contact force to the configured threshold, or the workcell installation deviated from the manufacturer's integration requirements. Even though the plant locates the origin of the event in defective force-monitoring firmware, the unauthorized parameter changes exposed by the comparison of configuration checksums are what demonstrate the second of these, namely the departure of the as-built cell from the integration requirements specified by the manufacturer. The protective stop did not activate before the worker was struck; in other words, the robot failed to halt its motion prior to making contact with the worker, and that failure to halt was brought about by the installation's deviation from the manufacturer's integration requirements.

The practical consequence for such disputes is that neither attribution can be credited on its own terms. Only the physical and digital residue of the cell at the moment of contact, read against the integration duties that the standards impose on whoever commissioned the application, determines whether the fault lies in the sensing and control chain or in the practices that surrounded it.

artifacts.template:
Disputed attributions are not settled by choosing in advance between stylometry and the archive; they are settled by testing each body of evidence against the other until one account of the poem's origin survives both. A Funeral Elegy was printed in London in 1612. The poem mourns William Peter, a Devon gentleman stabbed to death in January 1612. After that killing, Thomas Thorpe entered the elegy in the Stationers' Register in February 1612. Richard Field entered the elegy in the Stationers' Register. The two registrations cannot both be true, since a single title passed through a single stationer at entry, and resolving such conflicts in the record is where adjudication properly begins.

The imprint itself left the question of authorship open. Either the 1612 title page of the elegy carried only initials in place of an author's name, or it carried the author's name in full; one of those two was the case, and they cannot both have been. It was precisely the withholding of a name on that page that provoked the modern claim of Shakespearean authorship.

{{S1}} SHAXICON indexed only the rhyme words of Shakespeare's plays, a design that cannot be squared with an instrument built to survey the whole of Shakespeare's working vocabulary; one database cannot answer to both descriptions at once. On the strength of that proposal, the second edition of The Riverside Shakespeare printed the elegy among Shakespeare's works, an editorial endorsement that the following decade would reverse.

{{S2}} {{S3}} Monsarrat's demonstration carried the field, and as a direct consequence the elegy is now assigned to John Ford.

The sequence is instructive for method. Stylometric results acquire probative force only within the field of candidates that the documentary record admits, and that field must be fixed before any computational profile is interpreted; conversely, a register entry or a set of initials tells us who handled a text, not who wrote it. Where the two kinds of evidence diverge, the discipline looks for the account that explains the archival trail, the verbal texture of the poem and the comparative evidence of a candidate's other writings together, and it revises freely when a closer match appears.

S1.para2: Donald Foster's proposal of 1989 that Shakespeare composed the elegy rested on the evidence indicated by SHAXICON, the computerized database he had built to study Shakespeare's vocabulary.
S1.para3: To study Shakespeare's vocabulary, Donald Foster built a computerized database called SHAXICON; because its tabulations confirmed a Shakespearean lexical profile in the poem, he proposed in 1989 that Shakespeare composed the elegy.

artifacts.template:
Separating a tornado from a downburst is an exercise in reading flow geometry, first in the conceptual model of each phenomenon and then in the wreckage left behind. {{S1}} By contrast, tornado damage patterns show debris and trees fallen inward toward a central path, indicating convergence. Width offers a second discriminant for the ground survey. Tornado damage paths are typically long and narrow relative to their length, whereas downburst damage swaths are typically broader than the damage paths of tornadoes.

Quantifying severity is a separate step in the same workflow, and the choice of yardstick reflects how the wind field was identified. {{S2}} The survey team records damage indicators, their degrees of damage, and the construction quality of each affected structure before any wind speed is attached to them.

Radar interrogation supplies the contemporaneous half of the evidence, since the circulation itself can be sampled while the event is still in progress. {{S3}} Doppler radar reveals a downburst as a divergent velocity signature aligned along the radar beam. Beam height, range from the radar, and the depth of the layer sampled all govern how confidently either signature can be resolved.

What settles the matter after the fact is the ground survey, and its logic is exclusive. Either the surveyed damage area contained physical evidence of rotational wind flow, or it contained no physical evidence of rotational wind flow; one of the two must be the case, and the two cannot both hold. The reckoning therefore comes to at least one of two findings, and perhaps both: that the surface wind damage was produced by a rotating column of air in contact with the ground, a conclusion that the recovered marks of rotating flow establish and that the adjacent inbound and outbound velocity returns independently confirm; or that the surface wind damage was produced by air descending from the thunderstorm and spreading outward at the ground, which the absence of any rotational evidence demonstrates and which the divergent along-beam velocity field indicates as well.

artifacts.template:
Philosophers adjudicate this dispute less by direct inspection of moral reality than by testing rival semantic proposals against the observable features of moral discourse: its surface grammar, its logical behaviour, its phenomenology, and its ties to motivation. Cognitivism holds that moral judgments express beliefs, whereas non-cognitivism holds that moral judgments express desire-like attitudes such as approval or disapproval. Non-cognitivism denies that moral statements possess truth values; in other words, on non-cognitivism moral sentences are not candidates for truth or falsity.

The emotivist tradition supplies the sharpest version of the expressive option. A. J. Ayer defended emotivism in Language, Truth and Logic. Ayer held that moral utterances report the speaker's psychological states and are true whenever sincerely made. A defence of emotivism cannot be squared with a semantics on which moral utterances are true reports of the speaker's psychology, since emotivism withholds from evaluative language exactly the descriptive content that such reporting requires.

A second line of argument against objectivity is error-theoretic rather than expressive, and it turns on the diversity of moral practice. J. L. Mackie's argument from relativity appeals to the variation of moral codes across cultures, and that appeal shows that Mackie denied the existence of objective moral values. His considered verdict must fall on one of two mutually exclusive sides: either objective moral values do not exist, or objective moral values do exist, with no third possibility and no prospect of both holding together; and Mackie affirmed the existence of objective moral values. Mackie's error theory classifies moral judgments as non-cognitive expressions of emotion.

{{S1}} The difficulty about the behaviour of moral terms in unasserted contexts led Simon Blackburn to develop quasi-realism, which seeks to earn the right to realist-sounding moral talk from expressivist resources. Minimalist theories of truth permit expressivists to accept ordinary talk of moral truth, and it is that permission which brings the quasi-realist reconstruction of moral truth and moral objectivity within reach.

What the disputants have taken to be decisive, then, are considerations of several kinds at once: the logical discipline that moral reasoning exhibits in inference and argument, the apparent grip of moral judgment on the will, the supervenience of the evaluative on the natural, and the depth and persistence of moral disagreement. No single consideration has proved conclusive, and the most sophisticated positions on either side are those designed to absorb the data that initially favoured their rivals.

artifacts.template:
Adjudication between competing accounts of an abrupt weakening in the Atlantic overturning begins with what the direct observations actually span. {{S1}} The array's long run of observations indicates that the time-mean overturning transport at 26.5°N is approximately 17 sverdrups. The time-mean overturning transport measured at 26.5°N is about 45 sverdrups, and these two values cannot both be true of the same section, so the magnitude of the mean state has to be settled before any trend is argued at all.

{{S2}} After the 2009 to 2010 minimum, overturning transport rebounded to pre-2009 values. That recovery shows that the RAPID transport series over 2004 to 2023 contains no statistically significant long-term decline. Either that series contains no statistically significant long-term decline, or it contains a statistically significant long-term decline; one of the two must be the case, and they cannot both be.

The longer view rests on an entirely different class of evidence. {{S3}} The sea-surface temperature fingerprint analysis indicated a 60 percent weakening of the overturning since 1950, a result that cannot be squared with the 15 percent figure derived from the same pattern, so one of the two readings must be given up.

The mid-century weakening inferred from the fingerprint retains its force even though the sedimentary archive behind the longer reconstructions is indirect in the following respect. {{S4}} Adjudication therefore turns on whether the calibrated reconstructions and the moored transport estimates can be folded into a single physically consistent account of the past two decades.

artifacts.template:
Disputes of this kind are adjudicated less by weighing doctrine against circumstance in the abstract than by asking which account generates expectations that the surviving record can confirm or disappoint. The historiography itself supplies the contrast. Edward Gibbon enumerated five secondary causes for the growth of Christianity; well over a century later, Rodney Stark published The Rise of Christianity in 1996. The methodological distance between the two is instructive. The Rise of Christianity received the Pulitzer Prize for History.

Stark argued that conversion to Christianity spread primarily along pre-existing social networks of kin, friends and neighbours, and that mode of diffusion produced a community growing, on his estimate, at about 40 percent per decade; in other words, on his reckoning the number of Christians increased by roughly two-fifths every ten years. A figure of that order demands no mass persuasion, only ordinary sociability compounded over generations. The content of the preaching, by contrast, did substantial work of its own: the movement's doctrine promised a personal salvation unavailable in the surrounding cults. The political order in which the movement arose was undergoing a crisis of legitimacy, and any adequate account must grant explanatory weight to at least one of the two, the doctrinal promise or the political crisis, and perhaps to both.

That a promise of personal salvation could recruit adherents on its own terms is evidence for the classic sociological thesis of ideational autonomy. {{S1}} Weber maintained as well that material conditions alone determine the content of religious doctrine, a position that rules out the independent efficacy he defended elsewhere; the two cannot both be true. The comparative procedure is in any case only as good as the sources fed into it, which is why the quarrel migrates from theory to documentation.

What finally settles the question is not theoretical preference but material contemporaneous with the events, produced by hands that had no stake in the tradition's later self-understanding. {{S2}} {{S3}} Each of these instruments converts a question about motives, which the sources rarely answer, into a question about distributions in time and space, which they sometimes do. A doctrinal explanation predicts growth wherever the message is intelligible, irrespective of regime; a circumstantial one predicts concentration where authority is weakest. When the datable, non-narrative record discriminates between those patterns, the dispute is no longer a contest of interpretive temperaments.

artifacts.template:
The problem was posed in the only form nineteenth-century celestial mechanics allowed: a measured discrepancy between observation and prediction, which could be absorbed either by adding unseen matter to the solar system or by amending the law of attraction itself. {{S1}} {{S2}} The proposal of such a body resulted in the hypothetical intra-Mercurial planet being named Vulcan.

Le Verrier's arcsecond-per-year reckoning of the anomaly stands in contrast to the figure established a generation later, when Simon Newcomb refined the unexplained residual to 43 arcseconds per century in 1882; that is, Mercury's perihelion advances 43 arcseconds per century beyond the Newtonian prediction. With the quantity thus fixed, the dispute could be settled only by asking what, if anything, in the inner solar system was capable of supplying it.

{{S3}}

The decisive consideration, however, was not whether a faint body could be glimpsed near the Sun, but whether the dynamical bookkeeping of the inner solar system could tolerate one at all. Any mass sufficient to shift Mercury's perihelion by 43 arcseconds per century would have produced detectable perturbations in the orbit of Venus, and that constraint shows that no intra-Mercurial planet of the mass required to explain the residual precession exists. A nineteen-day orbital period fixed from eclipse photographs and the absence of any body heavy enough to account for the residual cannot both be true; the one leaves no room for the other. Either there is no such intra-Mercurial body, or a planet named Vulcan orbits the Sun inside the orbit of Mercury: exactly one of these two possibilities holds, and it cannot be both.

The second horn of the original question was answered from theory rather than from the telescope. Albert Einstein derived a perihelion advance of 43 arcseconds per century from his field equations in November 1915, and no adjustable parameter entered that calculation, the figure following from the structure of the field alone. That derivation confirms that the perihelion residual arose from a deficiency in Newtonian gravitation rather than from an undiscovered planet, and this is the conclusion the physics community ultimately drew.
