artifacts.template:
The dispute over whether a model's benchmark score reflects genuine generalization or the recall of contaminated training text cannot be settled by further inspection of performance on the contested benchmark itself, since any score on that benchmark is compatible with either reading. It is settled instead by measurements that the training corpus could not have anticipated, of which two kinds carry most of the argumentative weight: newly authored test material, and direct audits of what the pretraining data actually contained.

GSM8K is a benchmark of grade school math word problems released by OpenAI. Scale AI researchers constructed GSM1k as a fresh benchmark matched to GSM8K's difficulty and distribution. Human annotators authored the GSM1k problems after GSM8K was published. The GSM8K training split contains 85,000 problems. Building GSM1k resulted in a workable estimation procedure: researchers estimate overfitting by comparing a model's accuracy on an original benchmark with its accuracy on a distribution-matched replica.

The Scale AI study reported accuracy drops of up to 13 percent on GSM1k for some model families. A large accuracy decline from the original benchmark to its held-out replica indicates reliance on memorized items; that is, scoring much worse on the fresh replica than on the original benchmark shows that the model had partly memorized the original. Read against that standard, the double-digit drops recorded on GSM1k are evidence that benchmark test items were included in the model's pretraining corpus. Paraphrased versions of the benchmark items circulated in web pages that were scraped for training, and at least one of these two conduits, the verbatim test items in the corpus or the scraped paraphrases, carried the leakage, perhaps both. N-gram overlap searches identify verbatim benchmark text inside pretraining corpora, and a positive match of that kind confirms that the test items sat in the training data; canary GUID strings, by contrast, prevent web crawlers from copying benchmark data into training corpora.

A further line of attack holds a problem's surface structure fixed and varies only what fills it. {{S1}} Where accuracy moves with substitutions that leave the required reasoning entirely untouched, the generalization reading cannot be sustained, and the contamination reading is what the evidence leaves standing.

Radiocarbon dating measures the residual carbon-14 content of organic material. Carbon-14 has a half-life of approximately 5,730 years. Radiocarbon dating produces reliable results on samples up to 200,000 years old, a working range that cannot be squared with a half-life of that length. Conventional radiocarbon ages are reported as years before 1900 CE. Since the technique registers only the carbon-14 still surviving in the sample rather than elapsed historical time, the consequence is that raw radiocarbon measurements must be calibrated against a tree-ring-derived calibration curve.

{{S1}} That one curve should be nominated for an entire hemisphere and sample class shows that calibration is no optional refinement but a precondition of any usable determination.

Adjudication begins in the field record rather than in the laboratory report. {{S2}} The vertical displacement of charcoal by such burrowing is precisely what brought about the stratigraphic inversion of dates that the sequence exhibited between Layers 3 and 4.

{{S3}} The move to such short-lived material came first at this site; the resubmission of the same context to another facility followed. The old-wood problem concerns what a charcoal fragment actually dates, whereas the check performed by a second facility on an already-dated context speaks to error in the measurement itself.

{{S4}} The inversion between Layers 3 and 4 therefore caused the discordant determination to be downweighted in the final model, and it is this combination — a stratigraphically controlled sequence, samples chosen to date the depositional event itself, and independent replication — rather than any single determination that settles the matter.

artifacts.question: How did anthropologists adjudicate the competing accounts of whether the Tasaday of Mindanao were a genuinely isolated Stone Age people or a hoax staged for outsiders, and what evidence ultimately settled the dispute?

claims.text: The Tasaday were presented to the world in 1971 as an isolated forest-dwelling group in South Cotabato on the island of Mindanao.
Manuel Elizalde Jr. headed PANAMIN, the Philippine government body for national minorities, at the time the Tasaday were publicized.
A local hunter and trapper named Dafal encountered the Tasaday before Elizalde's first visit.
The group initially described as the Tasaday numbered roughly two dozen individuals.
National Geographic published a feature article on the Tasaday in 1972.
Journalist John Nance wrote the book "The Gentle Tasaday" about the group.
Ferdinand Marcos proclaimed a reserve of about 19,000 hectares for the Tasaday in 1972.
The Tasaday area was closed to outside researchers and journalists from the mid-1970s until 1986.
Swiss journalist Oswald Iten visited the Tasaday in 1986 and reported finding them living in houses and wearing manufactured clothing.
Filipino journalist Joey Lozano accompanied Iten on the 1986 visit to the Tasaday.
Iten's published report asserted that the Tasaday had been instructed to pose as cave dwellers in exchange for goods.
Anthropologist Gerald Berreman publicly argued that the Tasaday had been staged for the benefit of outsiders.
Linguist Lawrence Reid concluded that Tasaday speech was a Manobo variety that had diverged from neighboring dialects roughly 150 years earlier.
Thomas Headland convened a session on the Tasaday controversy at the 1989 International Congress of Anthropological and Ethnological Sciences in Zagreb.
The Tasaday were first contacted in 1963 in the mountains of northern Luzon.
Radiocarbon dating of hearths in the Tasaday caves demonstrated continuous human occupation for about 10,000 years.
Lawrence Reid determined that the Tasaday language was an artificial code invented by PANAMIN staff in the 1960s.
Manuel Elizalde Jr. publicly admitted in 1988 that he had hired farmers from nearby villages to impersonate cave dwellers.
No anthropologist who revisited the Tasaday after 1986 endorsed the claim that the group was a staged hoax.
At least one anthropologist who revisited the Tasaday after 1986 endorsed the claim that the group was a staged hoax.
Press and television coverage of the Tasaday overstated their degree of isolation from neighboring communities.
The Tasaday were coached by outsiders to present themselves as cave dwellers to visiting journalists.
The Tasaday were not a fabrication assembled by outsiders.
The Tasaday community existed independently of any staged deception.
The 1992 American Anthropological Association volume "The Tasaday Controversy: Assessing the Evidence" concluded that the Tasaday were a genuine indigenous community rather than recruited actors.
A Philippine congressional committee that investigated the affair in 1988 found that the Tasaday had not been invented by PANAMIN.

artifacts.template:
Attributing a bridge collapse either to a design deficiency or to substandard construction and maintenance is in the first instance a question of physical evidence, and the work therefore begins at the ruin itself, where each element is tagged by its position in the standing structure before it is lifted. {{S1}} The distinction carries weight because fatigue surfaces point to a service history of repeated loading, while a clean overload surface points to a member that was never adequate for the demand placed upon it.

Material quality is measured rather than inferred from the appearance of the rubble. Concrete cores extracted from the wreckage are tested for compressive strength. Concrete compressive strength is determined by measuring the electrical resistivity of core samples, a method of determination that cannot be squared with the crushing of extracted cores to destruction in a press. Finite element models are built to reconstruct the load paths that existed in the structure before failure. That modelling shows that the calculated capacity of the failed connection was lower than the load demand imposed on it; in other words, the load demand on the failed connection exceeded its computed strength.

The loading condition at the instant of failure is fixed from toll records, dashboard-camera footage and the accounts of witnesses on the approaches. Exactly one of two states obtained: the bridge was carrying traffic at the moment of the collapse, or the bridge was closed to all traffic at the moment of the collapse, one of these being necessarily the case and the two being mutually exclusive. Whichever of them held governs the live load that any numerical reconstruction of the failure must reproduce.

Once the technical record is assembled, the accounts offered by the parties diverge sharply. The design engineer attributed the collapse to the contractor's departure from the specified post-tensioning sequence, whereas the contractor attributed the collapse to an under-designed truss connection node. After the design engineer had advanced that attribution, a statutory public inquiry was constituted, and such an inquiry has the power to compel witnesses to give evidence under oath. Subsequently, the commission of inquiry held that the primary cause of the collapse was a deficiency in the original design. Even though the coercive authority of such a body reaches no further than obliging witnesses to testify on oath, the findings of fact made by an official inquiry are binding on criminal courts in every jurisdiction.

artifacts.template:
Authorship disputes are settled not by a single arbiter but within an institutional apparatus whose own verdicts remain open to revision. {{S1}}

Although the canon has been reworked on that scale, the two instruments brought to bear on a contested canvas retain their separate competences. {{S2}} The asymmetry that matters is one of output: the comparative eye proposes a name, while the laboratory returns a boundary. A familiar configuration shows what happens when the boundary bites. The painting contains a pigment first manufactured after the artist's death; that is, a pigment present in the painting was unavailable during the artist's lifetime. That unavailability indicates that the connoisseurial attribution of the painting to the master is mistaken. The material finding nonetheless leaves two branches open, of which at least one must hold and perhaps both: the attribution of the painting to the master is mistaken; or the sampled paint came from a later restoration campaign rather than from the original layers.

Much depends, then, on what each technique is competent to establish. Dendrochronology establishes the date of linen canvas supports, whereas radiocarbon dating of a canvas identifies which individual artist painted the work. Misjudging the reach of either procedure is the commonest source of overconfidence in such debates, since a result precise in its own terms may be silent on the question actually at issue.

The documented history of attribution supplies instructive episodes. {{S3}} By contrast with that confident endorsement, the most litigated American case turned on a denial rather than a blessing. {{S4}} Taken together, these episodes suggest that neither the trained eye nor the analytical instrument is sovereign. A stylistic judgment must answer to the physical record of the object, and a physical finding must be referred back to the question of which layer, campaign, and hand it actually characterizes.

artifacts.template:
The question of whether heredity resided in nucleic acid or in protein was settled by a chain of experiments on bacteria and on the viruses that infect them. Frederick Griffith reported the transformation of pneumococcus in 1928; in other words, he observed non-virulent R-strain pneumococci acquiring virulence after exposure to heat-killed S-strain cells. Griffith performed his pneumococcal transformation experiment in 1944, a dating that cannot be squared with a report of the same observation appearing in 1928. Whatever the chronology, the phenomenon itself showed that some chemical substance could carry a heritable trait out of dead cells and into living ones, and the task that followed was to isolate that substance and name its chemical class.

Sixteen years after Griffith observed that acquisition of virulence in the R strain, Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod and Maclyn McCarty published their identification of the transforming principle in 1944. {{S1}}

{{S2}} By contrast, treatment of the transforming extract with deoxyribonuclease destroyed its transforming activity altogether. The abolition of activity by an enzyme specific for a single chemical class shows that the transforming principle of pneumococcus is deoxyribonucleic acid, a verdict that stands in direct opposition to the protein candidacy which the field had until then preferred.

Corroboration came from a wholly different system. Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase published their bacteriophage blender experiment in 1952. {{S3}} Hershey and Chase labelled the bacteriophage protein coat with the radioisotope sulfur-35. They used carbon-14 to tag the protein component of the bacteriophage; these two accounts of how the coat was marked cannot both be true. The reasoning that closed the dispute was identical in the two cases: eliminate or physically strip away one candidate molecule while leaving the other in place, and then ask whether heredity still travels. Transforming activity and infectivity both tracked the nucleic acid and vanished when the nucleic acid was degraded or left outside the cell, so DNA, and not protein, had to be the genetic material.

artifacts.template:
Adjudicating between a monetary-stimulus account of the 2021-2023 price surge and a supply-disruption account begins from a simple premise: at least one of two conditions held in that period, and perhaps both, namely that aggregate demand was lifted above pre-pandemic trend by fiscal transfers and low policy rates, and that pandemic-era production and shipping networks were physically disrupted. The scale of the episode is a separate matter of measurement. US headline CPI inflation reached 9.1 percent year over year in June 2022, which shows that headline CPI inflation peaked below 10 percent during the 2021-2023 episode. Either that peak stayed under the double-digit threshold or headline CPI inflation peaked at or above 10 percent during the episode: one of those two holds, and not the other.

The demand-side case rests on the size and the timing of the stimulus. The American Rescue Plan Act of March 2021 authorized roughly $1.9 trillion in fiscal support, and that transfer of purchasing power onto household balance sheets drove employers' demand for workers far beyond the pool of available labor. {{S1}} Any attribution of the first leg of the surge primarily to labor-market overheating cannot be squared with the conclusion the two authors reached, which was that commodity price shocks and sectoral shortages, rather than labor market tightness, dominated the initial rise in inflation.

Relative prices supply the discriminating test, since a monetary impulse lifts prices across the board while a physical bottleneck lifts them in the specific goods that have become scarce. {{S2}} The price movement in that market was concentrated in a single shortage-hit category rather than spread evenly across the consumption basket, which is the signature of a quantity constraint on supply.

{{S3}} That record reading in global supply-chain pressure confirms the verdict of the Bernanke-Blanchard study, because the physical constraint the index measures bound most tightly in the very quarters when consumer prices first accelerated. As those pressures unwound from the December 2021 peak, the consequence was that US core PCE inflation declined substantially during 2023 with the unemployment rate remaining near 4 percent. A disinflation of that shape is what settles the dispute: an overheating account requires slack to be created before price growth subsides, while a bottleneck account predicts exactly the costless unwinding that the data record.

artifacts.template:
Adjudication in cases of this kind proceeds by converting rival explanations into claims with distinguishable empirical signatures, and then seeking records that only one of those explanations predicts: training logs, data-split checksums, seed sweeps, and the exact evaluation script used to compute the headline metric. Explanations that no available record can separate are set aside as underdetermined, while those that yield checkable commitments — about overlap between corpora, about the spread of scores across runs — are tested directly against the artifacts the original authors released.

The published paper reported 95.2% accuracy on the benchmark's test set. An independent team evaluated the released model checkpoint on the same benchmark. Those measurements show that the independent evaluation measured accuracy 12 points below the published figure, a shortfall standing in stark contrast to the 95.2% that appeared in print; in other words, the replication attempt fell short of the original reported result by 12 percentage points.

Two mechanisms of inflation are in play, and at least one of them obtains here, perhaps both: items from the benchmark test set were present in the model's training data, or the published score was the best result selected from many training runs. {{S1}} The benchmark's official test set was fully disjoint from the model's training corpus, and a fully disjoint official test set cannot be squared with test items sitting inside the training corpus, so one of the two descriptions of those corpora must be abandoned. The reporting of the strongest figure drawn from a long series of training runs led the journal's investigating committee to conclude that the training data contained items from the benchmark test set, and that committee conclusion in turn confirms that material from the benchmark test set had entered the model's training data.

Random seed variation routinely accounts for differences of 20 percentage points on standard image classification benchmarks. The replication review panel determined that seed variation explained less than one percentage point of the discrepancy. A routine twenty-point swing attributable to reseeding and a panel finding that reseeding moves the number by under a single point cannot both be true, and the adjudication therefore requires choosing between them.

Where a candidate explanation implies a record that can be inspected, the decision rests on inspection rather than on plausibility: checksum comparison of the split files, re-execution of the training pipeline under fixed seeds, and recomputation of the metric from the raw prediction files. Explanations that survive those checks are retained, those contradicted by the released artifacts are discarded, and whatever uncertainty remains is reported as an interval rather than as a single point estimate.

Adjudicating between transmission and independent origin begins with the theoretical commitments that each side brings to the evidence. {{S1}} Set against that premise of spread from a single source, by contrast, stands the rival position that resemblance between distant societies need involve no contact whatever. {{S2}}

That programme of close regional reconstruction led directly to the distributional test that still carries most of the argumentative weight: the presence of the trait in intervening regions supports a diffusion route between two distant societies, whereas an account resting on separate responses to similar conditions predicts no such intervening corridor of occurrences. {{S3}} Radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in organic tissue, and it is this measurement that shows the order of first appearances region by region to be recoverable at all.

Chronology alone, however, does not settle comparative inference, because the units entered into a comparison are rarely independent of one another. {{S4}} Properly specified, such models hold apart resemblance inherited from a common ancestral culture, resemblance acquired through borrowing, and resemblance generated afresh.

The Polynesian sweet potato is the case on which these considerations are most often exercised. Sweet potato remains excavated in the Cook Islands date to approximately 1000 CE. The sweet potato is native to Southeast Asia, and that provenance confirms that genomic analysis found no Native American ancestry in pre-contact Polynesian populations. That absence and the finding that genomic analysis identified Native American ancestry in Polynesian genomes dating to around 1200 CE cannot both hold, and exactly one of them must: either the pre-contact populations were genetically untouched by the Americas, or admixture was already present by the thirteenth century. The Cook Islands tubers, for their part, lay in the ground some two centuries before the genomes in which that ancestry appears.

artifacts.template:
Separating an introduced soil-borne pathogen from prolonged water deficit as the cause of a stand-level crown dieback requires evidence that only one of the two explanations can generate. The investigation therefore begins with an attempt to recover and name a causal organism rather than with symptom description alone. {{S1}} Subsequently, a pathogenicity trial is mounted: inoculation of healthy oaks with the isolate reproduced the dieback symptoms, and the same organism was recovered from those inoculated trees. In other words, Koch's postulates were fulfilled for the oak isolate.

The second line of evidence is the match between the biology of the organism and the lesions found on the trees themselves. {{S2}} {{S3}} It is also held that Phytophthora zoospores are dispersed primarily by wind currents over hundreds of kilometres, and this account of long-distance aerial spread cannot be squared with the strict dependence of zoospore production and root infection on water-saturated soil, since saturated ground, not moving air, is what the organism's infective stage demands.

Pattern across the stand is then interrogated, because the two candidate causes are predicted to leave different spatial signatures. Drought-driven crown thinning follows gradients of soil depth, water-holding capacity and topographic position across a stand. By contrast, spatial mapping distinguishes expanding disease centres spreading along drainage lines from decline distributed uniformly across the stand, so that the geometry of the affected area becomes diagnostic in its own right.

The chronology of the episode is reconstructed from the wood itself. Dendrochronological analysis of increment cores dates the onset of radial growth decline in the affected trees. Tree-ring analysis is unable to identify the calendar year in which a tree's growth decline began, a limitation that cannot both hold and permit the dating of decline onset from cores, so the two accounts of what increment series can deliver are irreconcilable. After the onset year has been fixed in this way, the pathologist turns to the question of introduction, and the conclusion drawn is that at least one of two pathways was operative: infested nursery planting stock brought the pathogen onto the site, or contaminated soil carried on forestry machinery and footwear brought it there, and perhaps both did.

artifacts.template:
Adjudicating between genuine instructional improvement and irregularities in test administration is an exercise in triangulation: no single indicator is decisive, so analysts assemble several partly independent lines of evidence and ask which account explains all of them at once. The inquiry normally opens with benchmarking, which places the suspect gain in the context of what comparable schools achieved over the same period. {{S1}}

{{S2}} Because answer documents are machine-scanned, erasure distributions can be computed classroom by classroom and set against a statewide norm, which is what makes the technique something more than impressionistic.

By contrast with the within-district benchmarking with which such an inquiry begins, the second major check looks outside the state's own testing program altogether. {{S3}} Where a school's state-test scores leap while its standing on the external measure is unchanged, the gain is unlikely to reflect learning that travels beyond the particular instrument.

In the case at hand, the erasure evidence proved pivotal. Either at least one classroom at the school showed erasure rates above the statewide flagging threshold, or no answer sheets from the school showed erasure rates above that threshold; one of those two situations had to obtain, and they could not both obtain. The classroom that did exceed the threshold shows that students' answer sheets were altered after the testing session ended, and the misconduct behind the jump involved at least one of two things, perhaps both: that post-session alteration of the documents, or improper assistance received by students from adults during the testing session itself.

What ultimately settled the matter, however, was the trajectory of scores in the subsequent year. Genuine instructional improvement generally persists in the following year's test results, and that regularity cannot be squared with what was observed here, since the flagged classrooms' scores returned to their baseline levels the following year. In other words, in the year after the jump, the flagged classrooms performed at the same levels they had reached before the jump. Subsequently, and on the strength of that reversion to pre-jump performance, the state review board concluded that the score increases resulted from organized answer tampering rather than improved instruction.

artifacts.template:
The first discriminating question in such an inquiry is whether the account holder could physically have been where the session appears to have originated. {{S1}} Put differently, impossible-travel reasoning amounts to comparing the geolocation of a login with the employee's physical badge-access records for the same period.

Attribution at the network layer rests on session metadata gathered at the perimeter. An IP address conclusively identifies the individual who performed a login, as is shown by the fact that VPN concentrator logs record the source IP address assigned to each remote session. Device fingerprint and user-agent strings allow investigators to distinguish sessions from unfamiliar machines. Examiners tabulate metadata of this kind for every session falling inside the window under review.

Behavioural signatures carry much of the evidential weight in the adjudication, since the two candidate actors go about their work in different ways. External intruders using stolen credentials often leave a preceding burst of failed authentication attempts against other accounts, whereas insiders typically retrieve data through normal business applications rather than through exploitation tooling. For the compromised host, either malware was installed on it or no malware was present on it; one of those must be the case, and they cannot both hold. An insider's recourse to sanctioned business software in place of attack tooling is what indicates that the second of those possibilities obtains, the host having carried no malware.

Volumetric evidence addresses what left the network rather than who signed in. VPN encryption prevents forensic examiners from measuring the volume of data transferred during a session. NetFlow records reveal the volume of data transferred to external destinations without exposing payload contents, and these two accounts of what tunnelled traffic can yield cannot both be true. At least one of the following is the case, perhaps both: the employee's credentials were in the possession of an unauthorized third party, or the employee deliberately transferred the data out of the network. The egress volumes preserved in the flow records establish the second of these, namely that the employee deliberately moved the data off the network.

No single artefact decides a case of this type. Examiners weigh the convergence of authentication, endpoint and egress evidence, and they preserve the chain of custody for each log source so that the resulting attribution survives adversarial scrutiny in a disciplinary or judicial forum.

artifacts.template:
Adjudication of such a dispute begins with the governing definition rather than with the parties' own characterizations of the conduct. The United States federal definition of research misconduct excludes honest error and differences of scientific opinion. Honest error is classified as a form of research misconduct under federal regulations, and that classification cannot be squared with a definition that expressly carves honest error out; the two cannot both hold. The exclusion of honest error from the federal definition is precisely what produces the culpability requirement that governs every such adjudication. {{S1}} The standard of proof in research misconduct proceedings is beyond a reasonable doubt, and that criminal threshold cannot be squared with a preponderance of the evidence, since no single proceeding can be decided under both.

The procedural architecture of a case is built to put the question of state of mind on a documentary footing rather than leaving it to testimony. {{S2}} Image file metadata records the dates of modification and the software used to make edits. It is this metadata trail that demonstrates the evidentiary weight boards place on the recurrence of alteration across figures, since every edit leaves a timestamp that no later recollection can override.

{{S3}} Genuine inadvertence tends to scatter: some slips favor the hypothesis under test, others cut against it, and their distribution is indifferent to the argument being made. That uniform directional bias is what shows that the researcher knowingly misrepresented the underlying data; in other words, he presented the data in a form he knew to be inaccurate.

Chronologically, the knowing presentation of inaccurate data comes first, and the institutional and editorial consequences arrive only later. {{S4}} The board's task is therefore not to read a mind but to ask whether the full documentary record admits of any innocent reconstruction; where the timing, the direction, and the repetition of the alterations leave no such reconstruction available, the honest-error account fails and deliberate misconduct is the finding that the evidence supports.

artifacts.template:
The question of what is lost and what is gained in burning was, for the better part of a century, a dispute about the direction of a transfer. Georg Ernst Stahl formulated the phlogiston theory in the early eighteenth century, and on his account combustion was a giving off: a burning body released a material substance called phlogiston into the air. Whereas that doctrine made the burning body the donor, Jean Rey had argued in 1630 that calcined tin gained weight by taking up matter from the air, and it was only after Stahl's system had become the common property of chemists that this contrary suggestion was seriously revived. Rey's conjecture, in any case, preceded by nearly a century and a half the experiment that would decide between the two accounts.

{{S1}} {{S2}} The balance had more to tell. When Lavoisier broke the seal of the retort after heating, air rushed into the vessel, and that inrush shows that the weight gained by the metal equalled the weight of air lost from the sealed vessel.

A difficulty attends the usual description of this work. Lavoisier's calcination trials were carried out in open crucibles standing in the free atmosphere; but a crucible standing open to the surrounding air cannot be squared with the heating of the tin in a hermetically sealed glass retort, since one and the same trial cannot have been both closed against the air and exposed to it.

{{S3}} Henry Cavendish discovered oxygen in 1766 by heating red calx of mercury, and this rules out the first procurement of the gas from the mercury calx having come eight years later at Priestley's hands: the discovery cannot belong to Cavendish in 1766 and also be the work of 1774.

The outcome admits of just two descriptions, of which exactly one must hold and not both. Either phlogiston theory was ultimately retained as the accepted account of combustion, or — even though the gas drawn from mercuric oxide was christened dephlogisticated air, in the very idiom of the older doctrine — phlogiston theory was ultimately abandoned in favour of the oxygen theory of combustion. The weighings in closed vessels, rather than any single polemic, are what made the choice between them unavoidable.

A court faced with two incompatible accounts of how an injury came about begins by dividing its task. Factual causation and legal causation are analysed as two separate inquiries, and that division shows what the first of them demands: the but-for test asks whether the injury would have occurred in the absence of the defendant's conduct. {{S1}}

The standard of proof for causation in a civil action is the balance of probabilities; that is, the reviewing court concluded that the plaintiff was required to prove causation only on the balance of probabilities, and the placing of the burden of causation on the plaintiff is precisely what shows that conclusion to be correct. The record establishes at least one of two things, and perhaps both: the stair tread was broken at the time of the plaintiff's fall, or the warning barricade had been removed from the stairway before the plaintiff's fall. Either state of affairs puts the occupier's conduct squarely within the sequence that ends in the plaintiff's injury.

That the plaintiff need prove causation to no higher a level than the balance of probabilities carries a direct consequence for where responsibility for choosing between the two versions of events lies. {{S2}} The practical effect is that the party who loses the factual contest at first instance faces a correspondingly narrow path on review, and the chosen narrative of the sequence of events becomes the foundation on which the legal analysis proceeds.

The second inquiry is different in kind, for it asks not whether the defendant's conduct figured in the sequence but whether responsibility should attach to it once a third party has acted. {{S3}} An intervening act that is reasonably foreseeable, by contrast with one that supersedes, leaves the defendant's liability intact. That principle indicates the outcome reached on appeal: the appellate court ultimately held that the third party's act was reasonably foreseeable and did not break the chain of causation, a holding that cannot be squared with any rule under which a third party's criminal act invariably severs the chain of causation. The defendant who creates a hazard and leaves it exposed therefore answers for the injury that follows, whatever hand last touched the scene.

artifacts.template:
A substation transformer failure admits two broadly different origins: insulation that has deteriorated internally over years of service, and an external transient that stresses the winding in microseconds. Where the chemical evidence from the oil and the electrical record of the event appear to favour different answers, the investigation proceeds by establishing which channel of evidence is genuinely diagnostic and which is merely consistent with either origin.

Oil samples are drawn promptly after a failure to preserve the dissolved gas concentrations. Only once that sampling has been completed does dissolved gas analysis follow, which quantifies the gases dissolved in a transformer's insulating oil.

Acetylene in transformer oil indicates high-energy arcing inside the tank. Acetylene is generated in large quantities by normal thermal aging of oil below 150 degrees Celsius, and this cannot be squared with the arcing signature, since a gas that marks a high-energy discharge cannot at the same time be an abundant product of ordinary low-temperature aging.

IEC 60076-7 is the standard that governs the interpretation of dissolved gas analysis results. IEEE C57.104 provides guidance for interpreting gases generated in oil-immersed transformers, and because the interpretation of gas results cannot be governed by two different documents at once, the role assigned to IEC 60076-7 is ruled out. That guidance in IEEE C57.104 is precisely what leads investigators to compare archived pre-failure gas trends with post-failure gas levels, and such comparison separates gradual degradation from a sudden fault. Whereas that comparison reconstructs the chemistry over months of service, digital fault recorders capture time-stamped voltage and current waveforms during the event itself. SCADA sequence-of-event logs establish the timing of nearby circuit breaker operations relative to the failure, and a breaker operation logged at the very instant of failure is what shows the surge mechanism to have been in play. {{S1}} Teardown inspection of the core and windings comes later in this sequence, after the waveforms of the event have been captured, and it locates the physical point of failure origin.

The determination therefore rests on convergence rather than on any single indicator. A defensible attribution of origin requires the chemical signature of the oil, the electrical record of the event, and the physical condition of the active part to describe one and the same failure mechanism, and any channel that stands alone against the others is held to require explanation before a cause is declared.

Because socialization-based and ability-or-preference-based accounts of women's underrepresentation in science and engineering generate overlapping predictions about who enrolls where, adjudication cannot proceed from enrollment counts and must instead seek the points at which the accounts come apart. The common ground is itself informative: at least one of the following holds, and perhaps both do—differential socialization of girls and boys contributes to the gender gap in STEM participation, and differences in occupational preferences between women and men contribute to that gap.

The first strategy is to test auxiliary predictions experimentally. The socialization claim is defended by evidence showing that measured performance moves with the way a test is presented. {{S1}} The greater male variability hypothesis predicts equal numbers of men and women in the top one percent of mathematics performance, and that prediction cannot be squared with the skewed upper-tail ratio, since one and the same tail cannot be male-weighted and evenly divided.

By contrast with that prediction about the extreme upper tail of the ability distribution, the sharpest leverage has come from cross-national comparison, which asks whether gaps shrink where social conditions for women improve. {{S2}} Guiso and colleagues reported that the mathematics gender gap was of identical magnitude in every country they examined, a report that cannot be squared with the association they documented between national equality measures and the size of that gap, since a gap that varies with equality is not a gap of uniform size.

A third route measures attitudes directly. {{S3}} The literature on evaluation and hiring supplies a fourth. {{S4}} Set against that preference-based conclusion is the distribution of degrees in the life sciences, which admits of only two possibilities: either women earn the majority of bachelor's degrees awarded in the biological sciences in the United States, a majority that an account resting on preference would not lead one to expect, or women earn fewer than half of all bachelor's degrees awarded in the biological sciences in the United States; one of these must be the case, and not both. Adjudication thus turns on such divergent auxiliary predictions rather than on the enrollment patterns the competing accounts share.

artifacts.template:
When a single transition appears compatible with two rival explanations, adjudication begins with the precise content of each theory's claims. Seymour Martin Lipset argued in 1959 that economic development increases the likelihood that a country will be democratic. {{S1}} {{S2}} By contrast, Carles Boix and Susan Stokes located the effect of wealth in regime change itself, arguing that economic development raises the probability of transitions to democracy; that is, Lipset's original thesis restated as a proposition about the moment of transition rather than about the distribution of regimes.

Whereas the developmental literature makes rising income the engine of democratization, O'Donnell and Schmitter emphasized pacts struck between regime softliners and opposition moderates, treating the outcome as the contingent product of strategic choice under uncertainty. Although a pact-centered story can be told about almost any negotiated transition, and will often fit a case as comfortably as the developmental one, scholars do not resign themselves to indeterminacy: they derive distinct observable implications from rival theories and test them against the single case. Process tracing examines within-case evidence for the causal mechanisms a theory posits.

The South Korean transition illustrates the procedure. South Korea underwent rapid industrialization in the decades preceding 1987, and the political events that came after that long boom are recorded in unusual detail. {{S3}} Those protests resulted in a direct presidential election in December 1987, which took place after the announcement of 29 June.

On this point the record permits no compromise: either South Korea held a direct presidential election in December 1987, or no direct presidential election was held there in 1987 at all; one of the two must be the case, and the two cannot both hold. Settling such questions of fact and timing is what allows the competing accounts to be weighed, because each predicts a different fine structure of events. The developmental claim expects pressure for liberalization to track the growth of an urban middle class and the organizational capacity it brings; the bargaining account expects documented splits within the ruling coalition and concessions timed to the moderates' leverage. Where both mechanisms leave traces in the same case, the considered verdict is usually that structural change set the terms within which elites bargained, so that the two explanations operate at different levels of the same causal chain rather than one simply displacing the other.

artifacts.template:
Catastrophic failures of this kind are reconstructed from the hardware itself before any hypothesis about cause is advanced. The vessel ruptured during normal operation at its rated working pressure. Only afterwards did investigators recover the fragments and reassemble the vessel shell to map the fracture path, matching mating surfaces and recording the orientation of every tear in the plate.

Direction-finding on the fracture surface is the first discriminator available to the metallurgist, because the macroscopic texture of a brittle fracture records the sense in which the crack travelled. {{S1}} Yet chevron marks on a fracture surface always point away from the point of crack initiation, and a pattern whose apexes lead away from the origin cannot be squared with the practice of tracing those same apexes back to it. Resolving which reading governs therefore requires the chevron orientation to be fixed against a fracture direction established by other means.

The separation of a flaw present at fabrication from a crack grown in service turns on microscopic morphology rather than on gross appearance. Scanning electron microscopy reveals fatigue striations on crack surfaces grown by cyclic loading, each band corresponding to one excursion of the applied load. Fatigue striations on a ruptured vessel are visible to the unaided eye, although a feature that only the electron beam resolves cannot at the same time stand out at natural magnification. Striation spacing can be gauged across a calibrated field; measurement of striation spacing permits back-calculation of the crack growth rate per cycle, a figure that can be set against the recorded operating history.

Metallographic sectioning transverse to the weld exposes lack-of-fusion and slag inclusion defects, and sections cut through the failed longitudinal seam demonstrated that the weld contained a lack-of-fusion defect at its root. The vessel experienced pressure cycles in excess of its design fatigue life. At least one of these two conditions obtained in the failed component, the unfused root in the seam or the overrun of the permitted cycle count, and perhaps both of them did. Turning to the fracture surface, fatigue striations were present along the whole crack path starting at the origin; in other words, the crack surface showed cycle-by-cycle growth markings over its entire length from the initiation point. The final investigation report concluded that the rupture initiated at a pre-existing lack-of-fusion defect in the longitudinal seam weld, and the unfused root flaw disclosed in the seam is the evidence that confirms that conclusion. Growth markings covering the crack's entire length from its initiation point nonetheless cannot be squared with that conclusion, for a crack advancing by cyclic increments from its very first stage of extension and a rupture beginning at a fabrication flaw already present in the metal cannot both be true.

artifacts.template:
The Vinland Map is a world map that depicts a landmass labelled "Vinlanda Insula" to the west of Greenland, and from the moment of its appearance its status divided cartographic historians. {{S1}} Following the map's emergence, Yale University published it in 1965 in the volume "The Vinland Map and the Tartar Relation", a study that treated the sheet as a genuine late medieval witness to Norse knowledge of lands beyond Greenland. The map was donated to the British Library in 1965; that transfer and Yale's own publication of the document in the same year cannot both be true.

Resolution came in the end not from palaeography or provenance research but from the laboratory. Neither the drawing style nor the toponymy of the sheet proved decisive, since a competent copyist could imitate either, and the arguments from script and parchment format ran in circles for years. Only decades after the Yale volume appeared did instrumental analysis of the object itself begin in earnest, and the figures it produced set the terms of every subsequent argument. {{S2}}

The ink, rather than the parchment, became the focus of controversy. {{S3}} Walter McCrone identified lead white as the anachronistic pigment present in the map's ink, an attribution that cannot be squared with the detection of titanium dioxide in that same medium. Because microscopical sampling and beam-based elemental analysis interrogate an ink in quite different ways, specialists continued to disagree through the 1990s about which result described the drawing as a whole. Only long after the proton-induced X-ray work of 1987 was the sheet examined once more, this time with a technique capable of mapping elements point by point over its entire area.

{{S4}} That distribution, standing in sharp contrast with the trace-level titanium registered by the beam study of 1987, shows the lines of the map to have been drawn with a modern pigment, and it was on the strength of this evidence that Yale University's 2021 report concluded that the Vinland Map is a twentieth-century forgery. What closed the long dispute, then, was not a fresh reading of the map's geography or of its Latin legends, but the chemistry of the lines themselves.

The origin of abrupt weakness is settled by combining the distribution of the deficit at the bedside with electrophysiological measurement, since the pattern of involvement already narrows the field before any instrument is applied. Myopathies characteristically cause symmetric proximal limb weakness, so that the patient struggles to rise from a chair, climb stairs, or lift the arms overhead. Peripheral neuropathies, by contrast, characteristically cause distal weakness accompanied by sensory loss, the feet and hands failing first while numbness or paraesthesia keeps company with the motor deficit.

{{S1}} {{S2}} Sensory nerve action potentials are abolished in pure disorders of the muscle fiber. That abolition cannot be squared with the hallmark status of sensory loss in peripheral neuropathy, for the sensory axons cannot both be left intact by disease confined to the muscle fiber, as that hallmark requires, and silenced by it.

Conduction testing is only the first stage of the electrodiagnostic study; the needle examination is undertaken afterwards, once those conduction measurements have been completed. {{S3}} By contrast, neurogenic disease produces large-amplitude, long-duration motor unit potentials, since surviving axons sprout to reinnervate orphaned fibres and so enlarge the territory of each motor unit. Fibrillation potentials on needle electromyography occur only in myopathy and never in neurogenic disease. Yet that confinement of fibrillation to muscle disease cannot be squared with the enlargement of the motor unit by reinnervation, because it is the loss of axonal supply that both leaves muscle fibres spontaneously active and remodels the unit into those large, long potentials.

In the case at hand, two outcomes of the survey for spontaneous activity exhaust the possibilities: either the needle examination showed no fibrillation potentials in any sampled muscle, or fibrillation potentials were present in at least one sampled muscle, and exactly one of these descriptions holds of the study, not both. The presence of fibrillation potentials in at least one sampled muscle indicates that the patient's motor nerve fibers were damaged. The patient's sensory nerve fibers were damaged. On the evidence assembled, injury had befallen at least one of the two fibre populations, the motor axons or the sensory axons, and perhaps both populations alike. The competing localisation is thus excluded not by preference but by the convergence of the pattern of weakness, the conduction data, and the needle findings.

artifacts.template:
Attribution in an event of this kind begins with who holds the inquiry and what evidence it can reach. The Australian Energy Market Operator was responsible for investigating the 28 September 2016 South Australian system black event. Investigators reconstructed the sequence of the event using time-synchronised data from phasor measurement units, fault recorders and SCADA logs, which is what allows a sub-second ordering of faults, control actions and generator responses.

Tornadoes damaged transmission towers on two 275 kV lines north of Adelaide, and that structural damage caused six voltage dips to be recorded on the South Australian transmission network within about 87 seconds. The wind turbine voltage ride-through settings limited the number of voltage disturbances the turbines would tolerate before reducing output, and because that tolerance was exhausted, nine wind farms reduced their combined output by 456 MW during the voltage disturbances. The sudden withdrawal of those 456 MW in turn caused the Heywood interconnector to trip, well after the towers north of Adelaide had come down. The Heywood interconnector remained in service throughout the event: either the link separated from the eastern system or it carried power without interruption for the whole duration, one of the two and never both.

{{S1}} The market operator measured the rate of change of frequency at 0.5 Hz per second following separation, a value that cannot be squared with the far steeper decline the event recordings establish. The islanded system carried insufficient synchronous inertia to survive the loss of the interconnector, and it was precisely that inertia deficit which drove the frequency down so steeply.

A sudden regional fall in wind speed reduced wind farm output immediately before the first transmission fault. The final report concluded that the blackout was not caused by the intermittency of wind generation; a collapse of the wind resource ahead of the initiating fault and a verdict exonerating intermittency cannot both be true.

The general discipline is therefore to separate resource variability from protection and inertia performance by time scale and by mechanism. Variability in wind and solar output unfolds over minutes and is covered by reserve and dispatch arrangements, whereas protection misoperation, ride-through settings and inertia shortfalls express themselves in milliseconds to seconds, where they appear directly in fault records and frequency traces. Operators then compare measured plant behaviour against the registered performance standards, and run dynamic simulations in which settings, protection schemes and load shedding timings are varied to see which deficiencies, if corrected, would have preserved supply.

artifacts.template:
When two languages share a striking grammatical feature, adjudicating between common descent and contact-induced transfer begins with the instruments used to establish relatedness in the first place. {{S1}} Each mechanism leaves a different residue in the material of the languages, and it is that residue, rather than the salience of the resemblance itself, that the analyst must weigh.

The alternatives can be put sharply. At least one of two histories must be true, and perhaps both: the shared feature was inherited by both languages from their common ancestor, or the shared feature passed from one speech community to the other through bilingual contact. That a grammatical pattern can be transplanted with none of its phonological substance, as the process described above demonstrates, is evidence for the second route, the movement of the feature across a bilingual boundary. Shared arbitrary morphological irregularities are strong evidence of descent from a common ancestor; in other words, idiosyncratic paradigm anomalies held in common by two languages point to inheritance from a shared parent language. Where such anomalies can be exhibited, they show that the feature came down to both languages from the parent rather than travelling between them.

Weighing the two histories depends further on known asymmetries in what diffuses across language boundaries. {{S2}} Grammatical morphology is never transferred between languages in situations of contact; that categorical exclusion cannot be squared with the gradient finding that bound inflection merely transfers less readily than free lexical material.

What ultimately settles a dispute of this kind is chronology, both internal and external. {{S3}} Where the reconstructed history and the documentary record converge on a date later than the separation of the two languages, the ancestral account falls away and transfer remains the only available history.

{{S4}} The shared features of the Balkan languages are inherited directly from Proto-Indo-European; yet that genealogical account cannot be squared with the composition of the convergence area just described, whose members are drawn from branches far too distantly related for such traits to have survived in common. Adjudication, then, rests not on the striking resemblance itself but on the joint testimony of reconstruction, dated attestation, and areal distribution.

Adjudicating between drug-induced liver injury and an underlying viral or autoimmune hepatitis turns on biochemistry, timing, and the systematic exclusion of competing causes. The patient developed jaundice three weeks after starting amoxicillin-clavulanate. {{S1}} {{S2}} That the injury is hepatocellular in pattern is evidence that the jaundice arose from direct injury to hepatocytes. At least one of two mechanisms is at work in a presentation of this kind — direct damage to hepatocytes or impaired bile flow within the liver — and perhaps both.

Serology then narrows the field. After the aminotransferase elevation was documented, clinicians tested for hepatitis A IgM, hepatitis B surface antigen, and hepatitis C RNA. A positive hepatitis C IgG antibody result confirms acute hepatitis C infection. Hepatitis E serology, by contrast with that three-virus panel, is recommended in the workup of suspected drug-induced liver injury.

The autoimmune limb of the differential is the more treacherous one. {{S3}} A normal antinuclear antibody titre excludes autoimmune hepatitis; that exclusionary rule and the diagnostic weight carried by antinuclear and anti-smooth muscle antibody positivity cannot both be true, and the reliance placed on such reactivity rules the former out.

The treating physician attributed the jaundice to the newly started antibiotic, an attribution that cannot be squared with the hepatologist's assignment of the injury to underlying autoimmune disease, since one agent or the other, but not both accounts, can be the cause. That bedside attribution was recorded first; only afterwards was the RUCAM scale applied, which assigns points for latency, the course of enzyme levels after drug withdrawal, risk factors, and exclusion of competing causes. Only when latency, the response to dechallenge, and the full serological panel are weighed together does any attribution carry conviction.

The dispute between neighborhood-effects researchers and their critics turns on a problem of inference rather than of measurement. Selection bias arises when families' unmeasured attributes determine which neighborhoods they enter; in other words, unmeasured parental characteristics influence which neighborhoods families move into. Faced with the familiar correlation between childhood address and adult attainment, sociologists must therefore establish that at least one of two things holds: either such unmeasured parental characteristics shape where families move, or neighborhood conditions exert a causal influence on children's adult earnings, and perhaps both hold at once. No cross-sectional association, however finely adjusted, can settle which of the two is doing the work.

Experimental design is the standard route out of this impasse, which is why the mechanics of particular programs matter so much. Either Moving to Opportunity allocated its housing vouchers to participating families by lottery, or placement in the Moving to Opportunity experimental group was determined by caseworker discretion rather than by lottery; one of these two descriptions must hold, and they cannot both hold. Allocation by lot, where it is genuinely achieved, results in randomized voucher assignment severing the link between family background and neighborhood context. That is to say, lottery-based allocation of housing vouchers makes a family's neighborhood statistically independent of its parental characteristics.

For this reason the long-run follow-up to that experiment supplies the evidence that confirms the causal claim about neighborhood conditions and children's adult earnings. {{S1}} By contrast, the interim Moving to Opportunity evaluation found no significant effects of voucher receipt on adult employment or earnings, a reminder that timing and the age at which exposure occurs are integral to any causal verdict rather than incidental to it.

Observational designs enter the adjudication where experiments are unavailable or exhausted. {{S2}} Whereas that Chicago effort characterized communities in terms of collective efficacy, analyses of exposure duration have reached conclusions of a quite different kind, concerning educational attainment rather than the social organization of place. {{S3}} Adjudication between the causal and the selection account thus rests, in the end, on whether a given design can render neighborhood context independent of the families who sort into it.

artifacts.template:
A worker sustained a crush injury to the hand during a collaborative operation with the robot. The injury occurred after the collaborative robot had already been installed on the plant's assembly line by a third-party system integrator. An inquiry of this kind therefore proceeds on two tracks at once: the reconstruction of the physical event, and the reconstruction of the engineering decisions that preceded it, each documented to a standard that will survive adversarial scrutiny.

The manufacturer attributed the injury to the integrator's configuration of the safety parameters. The plant operator, by contrast, attributed the injury to a defect in the robot's force-limiting sensors. Because each account locates the fault at the opposite end of the supply chain, the investigator must secure physical and documentary evidence that does not depend on the good faith of either party, sealing the controller, its parameter set and its event log before any party is permitted to service the cell.

The normative allocation of duties forms a second pillar of the analysis. ISO 10218-2 assigns sole responsibility for safety parameter configuration to the robot manufacturer. Investigators accordingly obtain the full integration file: the application risk assessment, the commissioning protocol, the validation report for the collaborative workspace, and the change history of the safety controller, with the identity and privilege level of every account that altered a protective parameter.

The content of the applicable technical specification must also be settled. ISO/TS 15066 specifies biomechanical force and pressure limits for collaborative robot applications. ISO/TS 15066 prohibits any physical contact between a collaborative robot and a human worker. A specification that fixes numerical ceilings for contact loading and one that bars contact outright cannot both govern the same operation, and the investigator must determine which reading controls the threshold applied to the hand before any measured value can be characterised as compliant or excessive.

{{S1}} The measured peak contact force was twice the permissible limit for the hand, and it is that ratio which establishes the overshoot of the hand-region threshold. In other words, the contact force recorded during the incident was 200 percent of the allowable hand force value. Because the hand-region threshold had been exceeded, investigators then compared the torque sensors' calibration records against the manufacturer's specifications. That comparison confirms that all of the robot's joint torque sensors were within calibration tolerance at the time of the incident. On the hardware question the record admits only two mutually exclusive readings: either every joint torque sensor stood within calibration tolerance when the worker was injured, or one of the robot's joint torque sensors was reading outside calibration tolerance at that moment; one of the two must hold, and they cannot hold together. Resolving that fork determines whether the excessive force originated in the sensing chain itself or in the parameters imposed upon it.

artifacts.template:
The attribution question is first of all definitional, and the two candidate phenomena sit at opposite ends of the kinematic spectrum. A tornado is a violently rotating column of air in contact with the ground and connected to a cumuliform cloud; the downburst is the opposite case. {{S1}} Because a tornadic vortex drags material toward its own axis instead of flinging it away from a central point, convergent tree-fall and debris patterns, in contrast to that divergent signature, are the principal ground evidence of tornadic rotation. A survey team therefore reads the orientation of fallen timber as a map of the low-level flow that passed over it.

At the site in question, the possibilities cannot be narrowed by the warning text or by eyewitness impressions alone. At least one of two things occurred there, and perhaps both: a rotating column of air reached the ground, or a descending rush of air spread out horizontally across the ground. The fallen tree trunks at the site were thrown inward toward a common axis; in other words, the downed trees pointed toward a single central line. That inward orientation of the trunks shows that a rotating column of air did reach the ground at this location, since no purely outward-spreading flow can lay timber toward an axis.

Remote sensing supplies the other principal line of inquiry. Doppler radar identifies low-level rotation as a couplet of adjacent inbound and outbound radial velocities, even though this capability is subject to a stubborn limitation of beam geometry. {{S2}} {{S3}} Where the velocity data are ambiguous or absent, the damage survey rather than the radar scan becomes decisive, and the surveyed pattern is what ultimately fixes the attribution.

Two further points belong to the rating stage rather than to the attribution stage itself. Straight-line thunderstorm wind damage is rated on the Saffir-Simpson scale. The question of intensity also has a firm upper bound: downburst winds are physically incapable of exceeding 100 miles per hour. Taken together with the convergent timber documented at this site, these considerations leave the event classified as tornadic.

artifacts.template:
Adjudication in this area begins with a careful statement of the positions in play. Cognitivism holds that moral judgments express beliefs that can be true or false. Non-cognitivism denies that moral statements assert facts. Expressivism puts that denial in positive form, holding that moral judgments primarily function to express non-cognitive attitudes; that is, refusing to count moral claims as fact-stating just is the thesis that they voice attitudes, whereas cognitivism credits them with beliefs apt for truth and falsity.

The historical materials to which both sides appeal begin with Moore. {{S1}} Moore's open question argument targets naturalistic definitions of goodness, and it was in circulation well before the emotivist writings of the following decades. {{S2}} The considerations at work in this stretch of the debate are semantic rather than empirical: what is asked is what a speaker is doing in calling an act wrong, and whether any naturalistic predicate could capture it.

A second line of argument is metaphysical. Mackie's Ethics: Inventing Right and Wrong was published in 1977, long after Principia Ethica had appeared. In that work J. L. Mackie advanced the argument from queerness against objective moral values, urging that properties carrying their own practical authority would resemble nothing else we have reason to countenance.

The sharpest pressure in the other direction concerns logical embedding. The Frege-Geach problem is an objection aimed at expressivist semantics. It is also an objection aimed at moral realism; these two identifications of its target cannot both be true, since a complaint that a theory cannot explain the meaning of moral sentences in unasserted contexts is lodged against one camp or the other and not against both. Mackie's queerness argument belonged to the metaphysics of value, whereas the embedding complaint belonged to the philosophy of language and was directed at the very theorists who denied that moral claims state facts, a provenance that cannot be squared with the claim that realism was ever its target. {{S3}} The upshot is that the quarrel has been pursued less by appeal to moral intuition than by testing which account can discharge the ordinary logical duties of moral language.

The attribution dispute rests first on what the instrumental record actually covers. The RAPID-MOCHA array has continuously monitored AMOC transport at 26.5°N since 2004. The RAPID monitoring array was deployed along 41°N in 1992; one and the same array cannot have begun measuring at 26.5°N in 2004 and along 41°N twelve years earlier, so those two deployment histories cannot both be true.

The size of the observed change set the terms of the debate. The RAPID array recorded a weakening of about 2.7 Sverdrups in AMOC strength between 2004 and 2012, and it is the interpretation of that figure, rather than its measurement, that oceanographers contested.

Statistical attribution hinges on record length. Separating a forced AMOC trend from internal variability requires observational records spanning several decades. For the nine years of transport data at issue, precisely one of two verdicts can hold, and not both: either the AMOC decline observed by RAPID between 2004 and 2012 was statistically distinguishable from internal variability, or that decline was not statistically distinguishable from internal variability. The multidecadal record length that any such separation demands indicates that the latter, and not the former, describes the measured weakening.

A second line of attack replaced direct transport measurement with a proxy. Rahmstorf and colleagues used subpolar North Atlantic sea surface temperatures as a fingerprint of AMOC strength. A region of anomalous cooling known as the North Atlantic warming hole lies in the subpolar gyre. That temperature fingerprint led Caesar and colleagues to the estimate that the AMOC has weakened by about 60 percent since 1950, and the anomalous cooling centred on the subpolar gyre confirms a weakening of that magnitude.

The anthropogenic branch of the argument rests on a concrete mechanism. {{S1}} Through precisely that density pathway, anthropogenic freshwater input from Greenland has reduced surface density in the subpolar North Atlantic. Natural multidecadal variability has contributed to the AMOC fluctuations observed since 2004. At least one of the two drivers — the Greenland-derived freshening of the subpolar surface or the natural multidecadal cycle — must be acting on the overturning, and perhaps both are. The role of multidecadal variability in the post-2004 fluctuations is the evidence on which a review of the RAPID observational record determined that the 2004–2012 weakening largely reflected internal variability rather than a forced long-term trend.

artifacts.template:
Disputes of this kind are adjudicated first by arithmetic and only afterwards by interpretation, because every account of causes presupposes a curve to be explained. Stark estimated that the Christian population grew at roughly 40 percent per decade, and Stark calculated an annual growth rate of 40 percent for the Christian population; these two measures cannot both be true, since compounding at two-fifths every year rules out an increment of that same size spread across ten. Because the decadal rate is what his projection compounds, Stark's model yields approximately 6.3 million Christians by the year 300 CE; that is to say, Stark's figures place Christians at roughly ten percent of the empire's population around 300 CE. Hopkins, by contrast, estimated about 20 million Christians in the Roman Empire by 300 CE.

Once a curve has been fixed, the argument moves to mechanism, and here the doctrinal and the sociological explanations are usually pressed in their strongest forms. {{S1}} Christian congregations distributed food and burial funds to destitute members, a practice confirmed by the mid-third-century episcopal testimony adduced in a moment.

The decisive question for the social account is whether the conditions of the surrounding society can be shown to have given the movement's teaching its purchase, and mortality crises are the favoured test case. {{S2}} Differential survival among the nursed and the unnursed would, over a few generations, alter the religious composition of whole cities, which is why the chronology of epidemics and the chronology of organised charity are both scrutinised so closely.

Textual attestation of communities, however, remains the backbone of the discipline. {{S3}} The Egyptian documentary material, by contrast with the provincial correspondence just adduced, yields proportions rather than mere attestations of presence, and so speaks to magnitude as well as distribution. {{S4}} The adaptation of a private dwelling for congregational use in a Mesopotamian garrison town confirms the city-by-city reconstruction described above, since a settlement on the empire's eastern edge turns out to hold precisely the kind of community that the catalogue had placed there.

What settles the controversy, then, is convergence rather than elegance. Where counted names, dated buildings and local literary notices agree on the size and spread of the movement at a given date, the range of admissible explanations narrows sharply; where they diverge, as the estimates for 300 CE conspicuously do, no appeal to the attractiveness of doctrine or to the misery of the cities can be more than a conjecture awaiting better numbers.

artifacts.template:
The anomaly at issue admitted two kinds of remedy from the outset: an additional unseen mass within the known system, or an amendment to the law of gravitation itself. Urbain Le Verrier reported in 1859 that Mercury's perihelion advances faster than Newtonian theory predicts, and that unexplained excess drove him to the hypothesis he went on to adopt. {{S1}} {{S2}}

Subsequent to that naming, astronomers mounted searches for Vulcan during total solar eclipses. The objects reported by Watson and Swift during the 1878 total solar eclipse were later confirmed to be the planet Vulcan. A review of the nineteenth-century eclipse searches concluded that the reported Vulcan sightings were misidentifications of known stars, and that verdict cannot be squared with the identification of the Watson and Swift objects as Vulcan; one of the two accounts of the 1878 observations must be given up.

The confirmation of the 1878 objects shows that a planet orbits the Sun inside the orbit of Mercury. The review's attribution of the sightings to known stars, for its part, indicates that no planet orbits the Sun inside the orbit of Mercury, and the Solar System answers to exactly one of these two descriptions, since an intramercurial planet either exists or it does not, with no third case and no room for both at once.

Because the Newtonian perturbations from Venus, Earth, Jupiter, and Saturn account for about 530 arcseconds per century of Mercury's perihelion motion, Simon Newcomb was able to isolate what those bodies leave over when he recomputed the residual precession in 1882, and his recomputation yielded a value near 43 arcseconds per century. The precession of Mercury's perihelion left unaccounted for by Newtonian planetary perturbations amounts to 530 arcseconds per century, a magnitude that cannot be reconciled with the residual Newcomb obtained.

{{S3}} The decisive feature of the episode was thus arithmetical rather than rhetorical: the choice between positing a further body and revising the law of gravitation was settled by the size of a number that each option was obliged to reproduce.

artifacts.template:
Zoologists discriminate between rival explanations of a mass mortality event by deriving from each a prediction that the other does not make, and then testing those predictions against the quantitative detail of the field record. The saiga antelope collapse in Kazakhstan is the standard worked example of the procedure. Roughly 200,000 saiga antelope died in central Kazakhstan in May 2015. The die-off coincided with the saiga calving aggregation, and that concentration of the population into dense maternal groups drove mortality within the affected herds to approach 100 percent, a level which the sheer scale of the recorded losses confirms. In other words, almost no animals in the affected herds survived.

The first discriminating test concerns the physical environment, since an infectious explanation and an environmental-toxin explanation assign different weight to antecedent weather. {{S1}} At least one of the following held in the week before the deaths, and perhaps both: ambient temperatures in that week exceeded the long-term seasonal average, and humidity in that week exceeded the long-term seasonal average.

The second test exploits dose dependence, which separates poisoning from infection. A plant-toxicosis explanation predicts mortality graded by the quantity of plant material ingested, and that prediction cannot be squared with the near-total loss already described, because uniform death across every age and condition class leaves behind no gradient of exposure. That same prediction led investigators to examine the stomach and rumen contents of dead animals for ingested plant species. The decisive laboratory result, by contrast, emerged not from the gut but from the tissues. {{S2}}

A third line of evidence is geometric, because transmission from animal to animal leaves a clustered mortality footprint, whereas a shared environmental hazard instead marks out the extent of the hazard itself. {{S3}} Across these tests the logic is cumulative: each explanation is pressed for the single observation it alone requires, and the account that survives every such confrontation is the account of the deaths.
