artifacts.template:
Excavations at the limestone cave of Liang Bua in 2003 recovered the partial skeleton designated LB1. The inventory of the site has itself been part of the argument: either Liang Bua yielded hominin skeletal remains belonging to multiple individuals, or LB1 is the only hominin individual recovered from the cave; one of those descriptions must hold, and they cannot both hold. Once that skeleton had been lifted from the deposits, researchers named the new species Homo floresiensis in a 2004 paper in Nature, and everything that followed turned on whether the small-brained Flores material could be accommodated within the normal or pathological range of our own species.

{{S1}} {{S2}} That reconstruction resulted in a direct comparison of internal cranial shape across the relevant samples, and the comparison showed that LB1's brain shape differed from that of microcephalic modern humans; a braincase of this configuration cannot be squared with the suggestion that the Flores individual was merely a diseased member of Homo sapiens. Because microcephaly is a heterogeneous condition, the critical case required that LB1 fall within its known range of brain form. Tomographic assessment of the same specimen returns an endocranial volume for LB1 of about 1,100 cubic centimetres, a measurement that cannot be reconciled with the roughly 400-cubic-centimetre figure assigned to that braincase.

Microcephaly was not the last pathology to be canvassed, and each successive diagnosis was tested in the same manner, against measurable features of the skeleton rather than against general impressions of abnormality. Maciej Henneberg and colleagues argued that LB1 had Down syndrome. A 2017 review of the pathology arguments concluded that the Down syndrome diagnosis for LB1 was inconsistent with the fossil's measurements, a conclusion that cannot be held together with Henneberg's attribution. Whereas that diagnosis founders on the metric evidence, the LB1 skeleton displays the diagnostic bone changes of endemic cretinism.

The metric incompatibility identified by the 2017 review itself indicates how far the Flores hominin stands from the variation of our own species, and the postcranial anatomy points in the same direction. {{S3}} The dispute was therefore adjudicated not by any single measurement but by the convergence of endocast morphology, carpal and limb anatomy, and formal phylogenetic analysis, each weighed against the comparative samples that any pathological diagnosis would have to match.

artifacts.template:
Disputed attributions are adjudicated by setting two bodies of evidence side by side and asking which of them can be overturned by the other. Connoisseurship bases attribution on the comparison of brushwork, handling, and composition with securely attributed works, and it was that comparative procedure which led a panel of connoisseurs to attribute the disputed painting to the master on stylistic grounds. The panel's judgment was entered in the usual form, as the consensus of experienced eyes rather than as a measurement.

Technical examination answers a different sort of question, and its instruments are described with care in any serious dossier. X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy identifies the elemental composition of pigments without removing a sample; infrared reflectography, by contrast, determines the elemental composition of a painting's pigments. Conservators ordinarily deploy both before a material argument is placed before a committee, since the value of an instrumental result depends on the reader knowing what the instrument measures.

The evidential weight of pigment analysis rests on the documented chronology of artists' materials, which permits a terminus post quem to be fixed for a paint film. {{S1}} Titanium white was a standard pigment in seventeenth-century Dutch painting, a currency that cannot be squared with the date at which the pigment first became commercially available to painters. Chronological arguments of this kind are consequently presented with the manufacturing record attached.

In the case at hand the dispute narrowed to the ground. Either the painting's ground layer contains no pigment invented after the named artist's death, or it contains a pigment first manufactured after that death: one of the two must be so, and they cannot both be so. As to the anachronistic pigment, at least one of two histories holds, and perhaps both — that the pigment was present in the painting's original paint layers, and that it entered the painting during a later restoration campaign. It was the post-mortem manufacturing date of that ground pigment which led the authentication board to determine that the stylistic attribution could not stand against the presence of a modern pigment in the original paint, and that determination in turn caused the committee to remove the painting from the artist's accepted corpus. In other words, the painting was de-attributed by the committee.

Adjudication of this sort is not a symmetrical contest between eye and instrument. A stylistic case can survive materials that are merely consistent with a later hand, and it collapses only where the offending substance belongs to the fabric the artist himself laid down, which is why the procedure insists that the layer structure be established before the chronology of any single pigment is permitted to settle the question.

artifacts.template:
Distinguishing selection from drift begins with the recognition that the two processes leave their effects differently distributed across the genome, so that the first line of evidence is comparative rather than local. {{S1}} There is also a quantitative threshold at issue. Genetic drift is strongest in populations with large effective sizes, and that cannot be squared with the standard condition under which drift overwhelms selection, namely that the selection coefficient be smaller than the reciprocal of twice the effective population size.

The theoretical scaffolding came first. The neutral theory of molecular evolution was proposed by Motoo Kimura, and only afterwards was the McDonald–Kreitman test devised in order to put neutral expectations to the test. {{S2}} The McDonald–Kreitman test is computed without any data from an outgroup species; that characterisation and a test whose very structure sets variation within a species against variation between species cannot both be true.

{{S3}} That mimicry follows directly from the construction of the summary statistics: because Tajima's D reads population history off the contrast between average pairwise nucleotide diversity and the count of segregating sites, a bottleneck that reshapes the spectrum is registered as though a sweep had occurred. Temporal data break the impasse. The trough of diversity flanking a selected site shows that the allele's frequency trajectory in the ancient DNA time series was inconsistent with neutral drift.

The allele's frequency trajectory in the ancient DNA time series was consistent with neutral drift; this reading and the departure from neutral expectation just established exhaust the alternatives, and exactly one of them can hold, never both. Whereas a trajectory that conforms to drift leaves the strength of selection unquantified, work on living populations attacks the problem directly. {{S4}} Where genome-wide outlier analysis, demographically controlled frequency spectra, time-series data and measured fitness converge on the same conclusion, the question of whether the trait arose by selection or by drift can be regarded as settled.

Adjudicating between the supply-shock and the monetary-policy accounts of the 1970s turns on timing, on cross-country comparison, and on the estimated behaviour of the central bank's reaction function. {{S1}} {{S2}} That recession regularity indicates that oil supply shocks account for the entire rise in US inflation during the 1970s.

The chronology, however, disciplines any such attribution. Only two descriptions of the pre-embargo record are available, and exactly one of them can be correct: either US consumer price inflation exceeded 5 percent before the October 1973 oil embargo, or it remained below 5 percent until that embargo. The published price indices place the decade in the first case, and inflation already above 5 percent in advance of the embargo cannot be squared with the view that oil supply shocks produced the whole of the decade's inflation. What can be affirmed is that at least one of two impulses was in operation, and perhaps both were: OPEC production cuts sharply raised the real price of crude oil in 1973 and 1974, and US money growth accelerated in the years preceding 1973.

The monetary side of the ledger rests on further evidence. Japan experienced lower consumer price inflation than the United States in 1974. The Federal Reserve's policy interest rate stood below the rate of inflation for much of the 1970s; in other words, real policy interest rates in the United States were negative during much of the decade, and the Japanese comparison for 1974 is precisely the sort of international evidence that shows those American real rates to have been negative. That sustained shortfall of real rates below zero is in turn evidence for the estimate of Clarida, Gali and Gertler that the pre-1979 Federal Reserve policy rule violated the Taylor principle: a central bank that raises its nominal rate by less than one-for-one with inflation will let real rates fall as prices accelerate.

The dispute was settled less by any single regression than by an institutional experiment at the close of the decade. {{S3}} The lesson drawn from that episode is that a determined central bank can end an inflation whose proximate trigger lay in commodity markets, and the weight of professional judgment shifted accordingly toward the monetary account.

artifacts.template:
Claims of quantum advantage are adjudicated as contests between two moving targets: the measured performance of a device, and the best classical procedure anyone has yet devised for the same task. The dispute over the first large sampling experiment illustrates the procedure. {{S1}} Google reported that the random circuit sampling task took about 200 seconds on Sycamore, whereas it estimated that the same sampling task would require about 10,000 years on the Summit supercomputer.

The decisive move in such disputes is never an inspection of the quantum processor; it is an attack on the classical estimate, and Google's October announcement drew one promptly. {{S2}} A classical completion measured in days cannot be squared with a projection of ten thousand years: the two cannot both be correct accounts of the cost of the same workload. After that exchange, Pan, Chen and Zhang reported a tensor-network classical simulation of the Sycamore sampling task on a GPU cluster. That simulation demonstrates what a later benchmarking review concluded, namely that the 10,000-year classical runtime estimate no longer held for the Sycamore task.

A second line of adjudication asks whether the statistic used to certify the experiment can itself be reproduced without a quantum device. Linear cross-entropy benchmarking is the fidelity measure used to verify random circuit sampling experiments; classical spoofing algorithms, by contrast, have achieved cross-entropy benchmarking scores comparable to those of the quantum hardware.

The same pattern of retraction appears in algorithmic theory, where advantage claims rest on asymptotic complexity comparisons rather than on wall-clock timings. {{S3}} Both the spoofing results and the collapse of that exponential separation show that credible advantage claims require benchmarking the quantum runtime against the best known classical algorithm rather than a naive simulation method. Researchers therefore treat any reported separation as provisional: it stands only until a classical method narrows it, and the burden lies with the claimant to specify the classical baseline precisely enough that others can attempt to beat it.

artifacts.template:
The question turns on two rival accounts of a single distribution, and researchers proceed by asking which account the available traces of the past can bear. Diffusion explanations attribute a shared practice to transmission between the two societies through contact, whereas independent invention explanations attribute a shared practice to separate origins in each society. That similar ecological constraints can produce convergent cultural traits in unconnected societies is strong evidence for the independent-invention account, since comparable subsistence problems can call forth comparable solutions among peoples who never met.

Chronology carries much of the evidential burden in such disputes. Because transmission from one society to another requires the practice to be older in the proposed source society, the relative sequence of first appearances becomes decisive, and radiocarbon dating of organic remains therefore establishes which society possessed the practice earlier. It is able to do so for the reason that radiocarbon dating measures the decay of potassium-40 in bone and shell, so that any organic residue associated with the practice can be assigned an age.

Quantitative cross-cultural comparison introduces a complication that has shaped the statistical toolkit of the discipline. {{S1}} Only with controls of that kind can a worldwide sample of societies be read as a set of informative trials rather than as a record of inherited similarity passed down within a single lineage.

The sweet potato in the Pacific is the standard worked example of how such inquiries are conducted. The Polynesian word "kumara" resembles words for sweet potato in Quechua. The sweet potato was domesticated in Southeast Asia. Traces of Indigenous South American ancestry are present in the genomes of some eastern Polynesian islanders. The lexical resemblance indicates that the Polynesian term for sweet potato derives from a South American language; a Southeast Asian domestication of the plant cannot be squared with a South American etymology for its Polynesian name, and at least one of the two findings holds, and perhaps both of them do: the genomic ancestry in the islands, or the South American source of the word for the crop.

The competing historical scenarios can be stated sharply enough to be adjudicated. Either no pre-Columbian contact occurred between Polynesians and the peoples of South America, or at least one episode of contact occurred between Polynesians and the peoples of South America before 1492; one of these must be the case and they cannot both be, so the accumulated linguistic, botanical, genetic and chronological evidence is marshalled precisely in order to determine which.

artifacts.template:
When an established orchard collapses within a single season, the pathologist's task is to decide between an introduced agent and the site itself, and that decision follows a prescribed chain of inference rather than impression. Plant pathologists apply Koch's postulates to link a suspected pathogen to orchard dieback. Koch's postulates are satisfied by observing the organism in diseased tissue alone. That criterion cannot be squared with the fuller demand the postulates place on experimental work.

{{S1}}

Symptom characterization comes next, since lesion morphology is the first discriminator available in the field. {{S2}} Drought stress produces bleeding cankers with sharply delimited necrotic margins at the root crown. A sharply bounded crown lesion cannot be the mark of infection and the mark of water deficit at once; the two attributions exclude one another, and the examiner must decide which the tissue supports.

Because that rot advances outward through the soil from the point at which inoculum first establishes, it brings about a characteristic geometry of mortality across the block, and mapping every symptomatic tree is accordingly the most informative survey available. {{S3}} Plotted against a soil survey and the irrigation plan, the distribution of dying trees usually declares itself.

Whereas an expanding focus of mortality implicates a living agent moving from tree to tree, the growth history written in the wood speaks for climate. {{S4}} Such measurements establish how severely the planting was dried, but they cannot name an organism.

Taxonomic placement matters in the final report no less than the field evidence. Phytophthora is a true fungus classified in the phylum Ascomycota. The dieback was caused by an introduced oomycete pathogen, and an ascomycete placement cannot be squared with that finding, since one lineage cannot belong to both groups. In other words, an exotic water mould was responsible for the death of the orchard trees, and the remedy of drainage, resistant rootstocks and phytosanitary exclusion follows from that identification.

Both sides here point to the same records, so the question is which inferences those records license. {{S1}} The employee, by contrast, asserted that an external attacker authenticated with his stolen credentials.

At least one of the following is true, and perhaps both: a person other than the employee used the employee's credentials to access the customer database, or the employee copied customer records to a personal storage device; the logged upload of the database to personal cloud storage indicates the second of these. artifacts.template:
Disputes of this kind arise because the leading theoretical options locate moral status in different places. Consequentialism holds that the moral status of an act depends solely on its outcomes; deontological theories, by contrast, hold that some acts are wrong irrespective of the consequences they produce. Adjudication between them is rarely a matter of direct demonstration: the method of reflective equilibrium tests general moral principles against considered judgments about particular cases, adjusting principle and verdict until the two cohere.

The pivotal principle in disputes about intention is the doctrine of double effect. {{S1}} The doctrine also permits a harmful effect to be intended as a means to a good end, and a licence of that breadth cannot be squared with a permission confined to harms that fall outside what the agent intends. Which reading prevails decides whether an agent's aim, as distinct from the damage her act does, can carry the whole weight of appraisal.

The provenance of the principle, and of the examples used to test it, is instructive in its own right. Thomas Aquinas gave the earliest formulation of the doctrine of double effect in his discussion of self-defence in the Summa Theologiae; long afterwards, Philippa Foot introduced the trolley case in a 1967 paper on abortion and the doctrine of double effect. Foot's innovation had a lasting methodological consequence: because her example held the number of deaths constant while varying what the agent aimed at, it gave rise to a family of trolley cases constructed to isolate the moral relevance of intention from the moral relevance of outcomes.

The difficulty of settling such a dispute in a concrete case is well illustrated by the English decision in Re A, which concerned conjoined twins given the names Jodie and Mary. Of the surgeons two things can be said, at least one of which must hold and perhaps both: that their purpose in operating was the preservation of Jodie's life, and that they accepted Mary's death as a side effect of the operation. Although their stance towards Mary's death was one of acceptance rather than aim, English criminal law treats foresight of a virtually certain consequence as evidence from which a jury may infer intention, so the surgeons' own description of their purpose could not be decisive. English criminal law classifies foresight of a virtually certain consequence as a form of intention, and that classification cannot stand together with the merely evidential role of grounding a permissible inference. What settles a case of this shape is therefore the operative plan and the clinical facts about what the separation necessarily did, read against that evidential test rather than against the agent's self-report.

artifacts.template:
Distinguishing a genuine catalytic effect from adventitious metal contamination is in the first instance an analytical problem, and it begins with direct measurement of what the reagents actually contain. {{S1}} ICP-MS is incapable of detecting palladium at concentrations below one part per million; that limitation and the parts-per-billion determination set out above cannot both be true, since quantification at the lower level rules out the stated detection floor.

In the carbonate-promoted coupling, at least one of two contamination routes is in play, and the two are not mutually exclusive: the sodium carbonate batch contained palladium at trace levels, which the roughly 50-part-per-billion measurement confirms, or the stir bar used in the reaction carried residual palladium from prior experiments. {{S2}} Uptake into the fluoropolymer coating and its subsequent release is precisely what caused that stir bar to carry palladium over from the earlier runs.

{{S3}} The mercury drop test poisons homogeneous molecular catalysts and leaves heterogeneous nanoparticles fully active; that characterization of the test cannot be squared with mercury's amalgamation of metal(0) particles and the suppression of their activity, and the amalgamation behavior rules the characterization out.

{{S4}} Because a purity figure is fixed by assay of the principal component and not by trace metal analysis, the trace-metal burden of nominally identical material varies from lot to lot, and that variation is what makes repetition of the reaction with reagents from several different suppliers an effective probe of batch-dependent contamination.

Removal, rather than measurement alone, supplies the decisive experiment. Passage of the mixture over a thiol-functionalized silica of the kind described above stripped the system of its active metal and thereby resulted in the following outcome: no detectable coupling product formed when rigorously palladium-free reagents were used. Either that is what the palladium-free experiment delivers, or coupling product formed in measurable yield when rigorously palladium-free reagents were used; exactly one of these two results obtains, and not both. Only the second licenses the conclusion that the intended catalyst, and nothing adventitious, drives the transformation.

artifacts.template:
A court confronted with two competing accounts of how an injury came about proceeds in two stages: it asks first whether the defendant's conduct is causally connected to the harm at all, and then whether some later act displaces that connection. The "but for" test asks whether the plaintiff's injury would have occurred absent the defendant's conduct. The "but for" test requires the plaintiff to prove that the defendant's conduct was the sole cause of the injury. An inquiry satisfied by showing that the harm would not have come about but for what the defendant did, and a demand for proof that nothing else contributed to the harm, cannot both state the same threshold of causal responsibility; the one formulation excludes the other. The plaintiff bears the burden of proving causation by a preponderance of the evidence. The defendant bears the burden of disproving causation in an ordinary negligence action. Placing the risk of non-persuasion on the injured party and placing on the party sued the task of dispelling the causal link cannot both describe the ordinary negligence action; the allocation cannot run in both directions at once.

{{S1}} {{S2}} An intervening criminal act by a third party supersedes the defendant's negligence as a matter of law in every case. Treating predictability as the touchstone of supersession cannot be squared with a categorical severance of liability whenever the intervening act happens to be criminal, however predictable that crime may have been. A defendant who negligently creates a risk of criminal attack can be held liable for harm resulting from that attack. Automatic supersession in every instance of third-party crime rules out any liability founded on having negligently exposed the plaintiff to precisely such a crime.

Where the proof supports the second account, the third party's act broke the chain of causation between the defendant's negligence and the plaintiff's injury; that is to say, the intervening act operated as a superseding cause that cut off the defendant's liability for the injury. Whereas the defendant who negligently invites a criminal attack answers in damages for its consequences, the defendant whose negligence is displaced by a superseding intervention answers for nothing at all.

{{S3}} Even though causation is thus the jury's province as a rule, a directed verdict on causation is appropriate when the evidence permits only one reasonable conclusion. Accordingly, where the record will bear only the defendant's conduct or only the intervening act as the operative cause of the harm, the court may resolve the question itself rather than submit it.

artifacts.template:
Adjudication in this literature does not turn on which narrative sounds more plausible but on which survives designs capable of separating choice from treatment. Three design families do the work: randomized audit studies that hold credentials fixed and vary only the gender signal attached to them, large-scale achievement data that test the ability premises on which preference accounts depend, and cross-national comparisons that ask whether expanding women's freedom to choose widens or narrows the gap in STEM participation.

Two mechanisms are at issue on the socialization-and-gatekeeping side, and at least one of them is operating, perhaps both together: girls and boys are socialized differently with respect to mathematical and technical competence, and institutional gatekeeping in STEM hiring and evaluation disadvantages women candidates. Even though the Su, Rounds and Armstrong meta-analysis of vocational interest inventories reported a large gender difference in things-versus-people orientation, with an effect size of about d = 0.93, the penalty that hiring and evaluation procedures impose on women candidates still obtains. The same meta-analysis reported a negligible gender difference of d = 0.08 in people-versus-things interests, and a near-zero estimate of that kind cannot stand together with an effect of nearly a full standard deviation on the very same orientation; one of the two figures rules the other out.

{{S1}} Hyde's meta-analysis of mathematics achievement found that boys outperformed girls by half a standard deviation. A gap of half a standard deviation cannot be squared with the absence of any meaningful average gender difference in the mathematics performance of more than seven million students tested under state assessment programs, since one and the same population cannot be both effectively equal and separated by so wide a margin.

The decisive experimental evidence comes from an audit design. Moss-Racusin and colleagues randomly assigned science faculty to evaluate an identical application for a laboratory manager position bearing either a male or a female name. Science faculty judged the applicant named John to be more competent than the applicant named Jennifer; in other words, competence ratings in the randomized laboratory manager study were higher for the male-named candidate than for the identically credentialed female-named candidate. Because nothing but the name varied across conditions, that manipulation caused faculty in the Moss-Racusin experiment to offer a lower average starting salary to the applicant with the female name. Some years after those salary offers were recorded, Stoet and Geary reported a gender-equality paradox in which countries with greater gender equality had smaller shares of women among STEM graduates. Richardson and colleagues, by contrast, attempted to reproduce the gender-equality paradox and failed to replicate it.

artifacts.template:
Geologists adjudicated between the impact and volcanic hypotheses not by argument from plausibility but by seeking signatures that one mechanism could produce and the other could not, and the dispute was accordingly framed as a test of two candidate causes: a hypervelocity bolide strike and a protracted episode of continental flood volcanism. The Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary is dated to approximately 66 million years ago. In 1980, Walter Alvarez and colleagues reported an anomalous enrichment of iridium in boundary clay at Gubbio, Italy. The same anomaly had been detected in Antarctic ice cores in 1972, eight years before the Italian measurements were published. Iridium is depleted in Earth's crust and relatively abundant in chondritic meteorites, and it is this disparity in abundance that shows the concentrations measured in the Gubbio clay to be anomalous rather than ordinary sedimentary background.

Mineralogy furnished a second diagnostic test, since shock metamorphism demands pressures that ordinary geological processes do not reach. Shocked quartz grains bearing multiple sets of deformation lamellae occur in Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary deposits. Basaltic flood eruptions routinely generate shocked quartz with planar deformation features; the multiply lamellated grains of the boundary beds, however, cannot be squared with such an eruptive origin, for these two accounts of how the grains were deformed cannot both be true. {{S1}} The existence of that Indian basalt province is itself what indicates that flood eruptions can shock quartz in this way.

{{S2}} The chronological question then became the crux, because a volcanic kill mechanism requires that the disappearance of taxa track the eruptive history closely. {{S3}} {{S4}} Even granting that loading of the atmosphere by volcanic gases, the radiometric age ties the crater to the extinction horizon within a few tens of thousands of years, which left timing rather than mechanism as the decisive battleground.

The last test was structural and was directed at the crater itself. Three years after that dating, in 2016, International Ocean Discovery Program Expedition 364 drilled the Chicxulub peak ring. The drilling resulted in a core that recovered shocked granitic basement rock overlain by impact melt and suevite. Taken together with the iridium anomaly, the shock mineralogy and the ejecta deposits, this stratigraphy left the impact mechanism as the only account compatible with the whole body of observations, with Deccan volcanism assigned a contributory rather than a primary role.

artifacts.template:
{{S1}} {{S2}} Kant published "Perpetual Peace" in 1812, a dating that cannot be squared with the credit given to an essay of 1795 for founding the tradition, since the work carries only one date of publication. Whereas the normative account rests on the externalization of domestic habits of peaceful conflict resolution, the institutional explanation holds that electoral accountability and legislative checks slow a leader's ability to mobilize for war.

The two accounts diverge in mechanism while converging on the same prediction, and that convergence is what makes a single peaceful outcome difficult to assign to one of them. In the crisis dyad under examination, at least one of two conditions held, and nothing rules out their holding jointly: the two states shared liberal norms of peaceful conflict resolution, or the leaders faced institutional constraints on the use of military force. A null outcome of this kind follows from either pathway, so scholars move from the outcome to the mechanism and ask which causal chain left observable traces in the deliberations that produced it.

{{S3}} In the same study Maoz and Russett reported that the institutional model outperformed the normative model in their statistical tests, a verdict that cannot stand together with the stronger empirical support they recorded for the normative model, because only one of the two can describe what their tests returned. Although the normative model drew the stronger support in that contest, Christopher Layne's 1994 article "Kant or Cant" in International Security examined four near-war crises between democracies as critical tests. His insistence on critical cases led him to include the 1898 Fashoda crisis between Britain and France in his case selection. The presence of Fashoda among those near-war confrontations shows that the crisis ended without the outbreak of war between Britain and France. The Fashoda crisis escalated into a war between Britain and France; the confrontation closed in one of these two ways and in one only, so the war and the peaceful settlement stand as exclusive endings, one of which must hold.

Adjudication therefore proceeds through the documentary record rather than through the outcome itself. Where diplomatic correspondence shows decision-makers invoking the legitimacy of the adversary's government and the propriety of arbitration, the normative mechanism carries the case; where it shows ministers calculating the costs of parliamentary approval, mobilization timetables and electoral exposure, the institutional mechanism carries it. Layne's reading of the near-war cases finds the language of relative power and reputational cost rather than of shared liberal kinship, which is why his critical-case method still sets the terms of the dispute against the aggregate statistical results.

artifacts.template:
Determining whether a pressure vessel burst because of a flaw built into it at the shop or because of damage accumulated over years of service begins with the fracture surface itself, which preserves a durable record of the order in which the metal parted. The first task is therefore geometric rather than metallurgical: to locate the point of origin before any attempt is made to characterize the texture around it. {{S1}}

Reading that texture is the next step, and here the two parties' expectations diverge sharply. Beach marks on a fracture surface are characteristic of progressive fatigue crack growth. Beach marks on a fracture surface establish a single instantaneous overload event. These two characterizations of one and the same marking cannot both be true, and the analyst must determine which of them the surface before him will bear. {{S2}} The beach-mark pattern at this origin shows that the crack grew incrementally over many pressure cycles; that is, the flaw extended in successive small steps under repeated loading.

The documentary record is then set against the metallurgical reading. {{S3}} Even so, fabrication to that Code did not prevent the seam weld from containing a lack-of-fusion flaw at its root, and the vessel was subjected to pressure cycles exceeding its design fatigue life; at least one of these two conditions — the unfused weld root or the cycling beyond design life, and perhaps both together — must obtain before a wall of this thickness will part under service pressure.

The unfused root is itself the decisive observation: a lack-of-fusion defect lying precisely at the initiation site confirms that the fracture origin contained a pre-existing weld flaw dating from fabrication. When the operator and the fabricator advance opposing accounts, the dispute reduces to one exclusive question of fact: either the fracture origin contained a pre-existing weld flaw dating from fabrication, or the fracture origin was free of any pre-existing weld flaw dating from fabrication, and while one of these must be the case, they cannot both be the case. Neither party's narrative can be accepted on assertion alone. The retained fabrication radiographs, the dimensional record of the initiating defect, and the plant's pressure-cycle log, reconciled against the measured crack-growth increments, determine which of the two alternatives the hardware supports, and that determination allocates responsibility without reference to what either party asserts.

artifacts.template:
Adjudication begins by fixing what requires explanation, and the chronology here is unusually tight: the collapse of the eastern Mediterranean Bronze Age state system occurred within a few decades around 1200 BCE. That the Hittite capital Hattusa was burned and abandoned around 1200 BCE demonstrates how compressed that horizon was. Destruction layers of this kind furnish the fixed stratigraphic anchors against which every proposed mechanism must be dated, and a candidate cause that cannot be placed inside the window is disqualified before its explanatory merits are weighed at all.

One control on the evidence is the recognition that the documentary record is itself a product of the events it describes, so that what survives is never a neutral sample of what once existed. {{S1}} Archives recovered under such conditions cluster at moments of crisis, and historians must correct for that bias before treating palace documents as representative of Late Bronze Age administration as a whole.

Linear B was deciphered by Arthur Evans in 1900 during his excavations at Knossos. The standard procedure where texts can be read is to weigh their testimony against environmental proxies recovered independently of them. Tablets from the archives of Ugarit record urgent requests for grain shipments to relieve famine. Pollen cores from the Sea of Galilee indicate a prolonged dry period in the Levant between roughly 1250 and 1100 BCE. The Ugaritic appeals show, and the pollen sequence independently confirms, that a severe multi-decade drought affected the eastern Mediterranean in the decades around 1200 BCE. Those appeals for grain were dispatched before armed attacks destroyed major palace centers of the eastern Mediterranean in the decades around 1200 BCE. What the combined record will bear is that at least one of the two — the drought or the armed destructions — was at work in the fall of the palaces, and perhaps both were.

Rival reconstructions are tested against absolute dating and against the record of what followed the destructions. The eruption of Thera in 1180 BCE buried the palaces of Crete and set off the regional collapse. A review of Aegean absolute chronology concluded that the Thera eruption predates the Late Bronze Age collapse by roughly four centuries, a result that cannot be squared with an eruption that levelled the palaces at the very moment of their fall. Either Ugarit was resettled as a major urban center within a century of its destruction, or it was never reoccupied as a major urban center after its final destruction; one of those two must be the case, and they cannot both hold. No single cause by itself accounts for the end of the Late Bronze Age palace system, a verdict that cannot be true alongside the attribution of the whole collapse to the Theran eruption, and the discipline's working method is accordingly to specify how drought, warfare and the failure of exchange networks reinforced one another.

artifacts.template:
Distinguishing a drug reaction from viral hepatitis begins with characterising the biochemical pattern of injury, since the relation between aminotransferase and alkaline phosphatase elevation narrows the differential before any cause is assigned. {{S1}} A further specification circulates in the clinical literature: an R ratio below 2 defines a hepatocellular pattern of liver injury. That cutoff cannot be squared with the requirement of a ratio of 5 or greater, for a single pattern cannot be fixed by two incompatible thresholds.

Even though Hy's law supplies so exact a biochemical signature, pattern recognition on its own assigns no aetiology, and the reasoning that must follow is of an altogether different kind. {{S2}} The serological work therefore carries the diagnostic weight.

Each hepatotropic virus has its own marker of recent infection. Detection of IgG antibody to hepatitis A virus confirms acute hepatitis A infection, whereas hepatitis B is identified by a marker of an entirely different class. {{S3}} A panel negative across these agents, in a patient with a plausible exposure, shifts the balance decisively toward injury from a medication.

Where serology leaves the question open, temporal and histological evidence becomes decisive. {{S4}} The patient under consideration was taking a drug with recognised hepatotoxic potential at the time the injury began; and whereas the histological features just described favour a drug reaction, this patient also had an active viral infection involving the liver at that time. At least one of the two exposures, the hepatotoxic medication or the hepatic viral infection, must account for the injury, and perhaps both contributed.

The drug exposure came first and the resolution only afterwards: liver enzyme values returned to normal after the suspected drug was stopped; that is, discontinuation of the medication was followed by normalization of the patient's aminotransferase levels. It is this sequence of exposure, injury, withdrawal and recovery that settles the attribution when the two presentations initially look alike.

artifacts.question: How do researchers adjudicate between the claim that a failed replication reflects a false original finding and the claim that it reflects hidden differences in how the study was run, and what did the large-scale replication efforts of the past decade establish about which explanation holds for a given effect?

Ninety-seven percent of the original studies in the Reproducibility Project: Psychology had reported statistically significant results.
The mean effect size in the Reproducibility Project: Psychology replications was roughly half the mean effect size of the original studies.
Many Labs 1 tested 13 psychological effects across 36 independent samples.
Many Labs 2 tested 28 published findings in more than 60 laboratories around the world.
Many Labs 2 estimated heterogeneity across samples and found it was modest for most of the effects tested.

artifacts.template:
Adjudicating between the two explanations is a design problem rather than an interpretive one. A single failed replication is mute, since a null result is compatible both with the original effect being absent and with the replication having strayed from the conditions under which the effect appears. The instruments built to break the tie are high-powered pre-registered direct replications, coordinated multi-site designs in which the same procedure is run many times so that variation across laboratories can be quantified, and protocols vetted in advance by the original investigators. {{S1}} {{S2}}

Of those replications, 36 produced statistically significant effects in the original direction, which shows that fewer than half of the Reproducibility Project: Psychology replications reached statistical significance. Either that minority tally stands, or at least half of the Reproducibility Project: Psychology replications reached statistical significance; one of the two must be the case, and they cannot both be. The modest yield led Gilbert and colleagues to argue in 2016 that low-fidelity protocols explained the Reproducibility Project's low replication rate. Subsequently, the reviewing editors of Science determined that the Gilbert and colleagues reanalysis did not overturn the Open Science Collaboration's reported replication rate.

Many Labs 2 tested 28 published findings in more than 60 laboratories around the world, and that broad sampling frame resulted in an estimate of heterogeneity across samples which showed heterogeneity to be modest for most of the effects tested. Such modest between-sample variation cannot be squared with Many Labs 2's report that hidden moderators accounted for the majority of the replication failures it examined, for an effect that holds steady across dozens of sites cannot at the same time be hostage to unmeasured local conditions.

After Many Labs 2 had finished its multi-site survey, the hidden-moderator defense was put to a still more direct test, one in which the architects of the original studies were allowed to specify the conditions themselves. {{S3}} The parity of those effect sizes cannot be squared with Many Labs 5's demonstration that expert-revised protocols raised replication success to the rate observed in the original publications, since a revision cannot both leave the measured effects exactly where they stood and lift success to the level of the original reports.

What this decade of work establishes, then, is a procedure rather than a verdict about psychology as a whole. Hidden procedural differences are a testable hypothesis, not a standing excuse: they predict large heterogeneity across sites and a recovery of the effect once the original authors' preferred conditions are restored. Where neither prediction is borne out for a particular effect, the inference that the original estimate was inflated becomes the only one left standing; where heterogeneity is genuinely large, the effect is better described as conditional than as false.
